definition_zh: 闯入；侵扰；打扰；干涉；侵入（地质）
definition_en: the act of entering a place, situation, or private life where you are not wanted or allowed
core_image: 一扇门被从外面推开，站在屋里的人被硬闯进来
scene: 正与友人视频通话时，房门忽然被推开，镜头里闯进来一个陌生人。Somebody pushed the door open and forced an intrusion into the room during the call.
sceneCN: 这里 intrusion 是「闯入；侵扰」（第 1 个义项：未经允许地进入某处），场景句表现为突然闯进私人空间，句意：视频通话时房间突然被外人闯入。

derivatives.zh: 基础动词，义为「闯入；打扰」
基础词加后缀 -ive 构成，义为「侵入的；打扰的」
加后缀 -er 构成，义为「闯入者」
加后缀 -ist 构成，义为「干涉主义者」

senses.title: An unwanted entry into a place
senses.definition: the act of entering a place or building where you are not allowed or welcome
senses.definitionCN: 进入某地或某建筑，而该处并不允许或欢迎你
senses.example: Guards reported an intrusion into the laboratory.
senses.exampleCN: 警卫报告有人闯入了实验室。
senses.why: The core image is a body pushing in against a barrier, so the noun first names a physical entry that is not wanted.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是身体顶着阻隔往里挤，所以这个词先指不受欢迎的物理性进入。

senses.title: Interference in private life
senses.definition: an unwanted disturbance of another person private affairs, such as privacy or family life
senses.definitionCN: 对他人私事（如隐私或家庭生活）不受欢迎的干扰
senses.example: Some people feel that reporters make an intrusion into private life.
senses.exampleCN: 因此：有些人觉得记者侵扰了私生活。
senses.why: Once the barrier is personal space rather than a wall, the same pushing-in becomes an offence to privacy.
senses.whyCN: 当阻隔不再是墙而是个人空间时，同样的往里挤就变成对隐私的侵犯。

senses.title: An interruption that bothers
senses.definition: a sudden interruption that annoys people who are busy or in private
senses.definitionCN: 突然打断别人的事情，让忙碌或私处的人不快
senses.example: She knocked politely before making her intrusion.
senses.exampleCN: 她在冒昧打扰之前先礼貌地敲了门。
senses.why: A call or knock arriving at the wrong moment carries the same unwanted entry into the attention of someone else.
senses.whyCN: 电话或敲门在不恰当的时刻到达，同样是未经允许进入他人的注意力，所以这个词也指打扰。

senses.title: Interference in another person affairs
senses.definition: the act of becoming involved in a dispute or system that does not belong to the speaker
senses.definitionCN: 介入本不属于自己的争端或系统
senses.example: Neighbours objected to the intrusion of regulators into the dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 邻居们反对监管机构介入这场纠纷。
senses.why: Entering a decision or dispute that is not yours repeats the core push into forbidden ground, now in the realm of authority.
senses.whyCN: 进入本不属于自己的决定或争端，是「闯入禁区」在权力层面的重演，所以这个词也指干涉。

senses.title: A body forcing its way into rock
senses.definition: the forcing of molten rock into existing layers, or the rock body so formed
senses.definitionCN: 熔岩挤入已有岩层的过程，或由此形成的岩体
senses.example: The cliff shows a dark igneous intrusion.
senses.exampleCN: 这处崖壁上可见一条深色的火成侵入体。
senses.why: Geology borrowed the everyday push-in image for magma pressing into older rock from below.
senses.whyCN: 地质学借用日常的「往里挤」意象，指岩浆自下而上压入更老的岩层，所以这个词也有地质义。

senses.title: An unwanted sound in pronunciation
senses.definition: a sound added between other sounds in speech, often by accident
senses.definitionCN: 说话时在两个音之间多出来的、常属无意的一个音
senses.example: The extra sound is a linguistic intrusion.
senses.exampleCN: 这个多出来的音属于一种增音现象。
senses.why: A sound that slips between two neighbours behaves like an unwanted visitor squeezing into a crowded room.
senses.whyCN: 一个音溜进两个相邻音之间，就像不速之客挤进已经坐满的房间，所以这个词也指增音。

intro.en: Intrusion comes from Latin intrusionem, a pushing in, from intrudere, to thrust or push into.
intro.cn: intrusion 来自拉丁语 intrusionem（往里推），源于 intrudere（推入、硬塞）。

items.en: Trudere is a verb meaning to thrust or push.
items.cn: trudere 是动词，意为推、挤。

items.en: Intrudere adds in- to trudere and means to push into.
items.cn: intrudere 在 trudere 前加 in-，意为推入。

items.en: Intrusionem is the action noun form of the same verb.
items.cn: intrusionem 是同一动词的动作名词形式。

items.en: The form intrusion passes through Old French.
items.cn: 形式 intrusion 经古法语传入。

items.en: Intrusion names an unlawful taking of lands in property law.
items.cn: 中古英语借入后先指非法侵占地权的不当占有（财产法中的用语）。

items.en: Modern English extends the word to privacy, sound, and geology.
items.cn: 现代英语把这一词扩展到隐私、语音与地质领域。

note.en: Intrusion sits with the verb intrude and the adjective intrusive, and near trespass, interference, and invasion.
note.cn: intrusion 与动词 intrude、形容词 intrusive 同族，近义区有 trespass、interference、invasion。

entries.definition: to push in where one is not wanted
pushing in undesirably
a person who breaks in
a supporter of interference
entries.definitionCN: 主张干涉他人事务的人

entries.definition: wrongful entry onto land that belongs to another
the act of getting involved where one is not needed
an entrance by force on a large scale

normalIntro.en: Take the verb intrude, drop the final -de and add -sion: the family cluster intrude, intrusive, intrusion tells the story.
normalIntro.cn: 把 intrude 的尾 -de 换成 -sion 就是 intrusion；intrude、intrusive、intrusion 这一族词共同讲「往里挤」。

normal.en: Intrusion belongs to the -sion family of action nouns, as in intrusion, revision, and decision.
normal.cn: intrusion 属于以 -sion 结尾的动作名词族，与 revision、decision 同理。

normal.en: The stem trud- means push, so every member of the family carries the idea of shoving in.
normal.cn: 词干 trud- 意为「推」，所以整族词都带「往里挤」之意。

normal.en: Intrude is the verb, intrusive the adjective, intruder the person, intrusion the act.
normal.cn: intrude 是动词，intrusive 是形容词，intruder 是人，intrusion 是行为本身。

normal.en: Pair it with the prefix in-, as in income and intake, both of which point inward.
normal.cn: 注意前缀 in-，与 income、intake 一样都指「向里」。

normal.en: In geology the word marks magma pushed into other rock layers.
normal.cn: 在地质学里，这个词指岩浆挤入其他岩层。

abstract.en: Picture a stranger opening your office door without knocking.
abstract.cn: 想象一个陌生人没敲门就推开了你的办公室门。

abstract.en: Imagine a hand sliding a paper into a sealed file.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把一张纸塞进已经封好的档案袋。

abstract.en: See a crimson thread of magma squeezing between grey rock layers.
abstract.cn: 想象一条暗红色岩浆挤进灰色岩层之间。

examples.en: The company won a case about intrusion into private emails.
examples.cn: 这家公司赢得了那起关于侵犯私人邮件的案件。

examples.en: Remote cameras reduce human intrusion into wildlife sanctuaries.
examples.cn: 远程摄像机减少了人类对野生动物保护区的干扰。

examples.en: Each sudden intrusion at the meeting was greeted with a sigh.
examples.cn: 会上每一次突然的打断都换来一声叹气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬蹿」——一声硬闯着蹿进来，就是闯入、打搅；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（向里）+ trudere（推）→ intrudere（推入）→ intrusionem（推进）→ 古法语 intrusion → 英语 intrusion，核心义「硬往里挤」。

sensesIntro.en: Intrusion begins as a body pushing into a place, then spreads to privacy, interruption, authority, rock, and sound.
sensesIntro.cn: intrusion 从身体硬挤进一个地点开始，随后扩展到隐私、打断、权力干预，以及岩石与语音领域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door forced open from the outside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇门被从外面硬推开。

branches.en: A physical entry into a place is the first sense.
branches.cn: 进入某地的物理闯入是第一义项。

branches.en: Private space and attention turn entry into offence and interruption.
branches.cn: 私人空间与注意力让「进入」变成对隐私的冒犯与打断。

branches.en: Authority becomes the new barrier in the interference sense.
branches.cn: 在干涉义中，阻隔变成了职权边界。

branches.en: Magma pushing into older rock repeats the physical image in geology.
branches.cn: 岩浆挤入更老岩层，是物理意象在地质学的复现。

branches.en: A sound slipping between others is an entry that crosses a boundary too.
branches.cn: 一个音溜进其他音之间，同样是一次越界的进入。

intro.en: Intrusion is built from the prefix in- and the Latin stem trud-, which means push.
intro.cn: intrusion 由前缀 in- 与拉丁词干 trud-（推）构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin in- means in or into, and trudere means to push; together they mean to push in.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 in- 意为「向内」，trudere 意为「推」，合起来就是「推入」。

items.example: The prefix in- adds direction inward.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 表示向内的方向。

items.example: Trudere supplies the pushing image.
items.exampleCN: trudere 提供「推」的意象。

items.example: Intrudere joins prefix and stem.
items.exampleCN: intrudere 由前缀与词干结合而成。

items.example: Intrusion keeps the action-sense of the stem.
items.exampleCN: intrusion 保留词干的动作含义。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或过程的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -sion turns the verb into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -sion 把动词变为名词。

items.example: Intrude is the everyday verb side.
items.exampleCN: intrude 是日常使用的动词形式。

items.meaningCN: 表示具有某倾向的形容词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ive forms intrusive.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ive 构成 intrusive。

items.example: The suffix -er forms intruder.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 intruder。

items.example: Intrusive describes a person or question.
items.exampleCN: intrusive 形容人或问题冒失。

items.example: Intruder names the person.
items.exampleCN: intruder 指闯入的人。

definition_zh: 侵入的；打扰的；爱打听的；冒失的；（地质）侵入的
definition_en: affecting something or someone in an unwanted and annoying way, especially by entering private matters
core_image: 一只手指尖戳进别人本来关着的抽屉里
scene: 有人总爱追问同事的工资和家里的事，让谁都不自在。Somebody keeps asking intrusive questions about pay and home life.
sceneCN: 这里 intrusive 是「侵扰的；爱打听的」（第 1 个义项：以令人不适的方式介入他人私事），句意：有人总想打听别人的私事，令人不适。

derivatives.zh: 基础词加后缀 -ion 构成，义为「闯入；侵扰」
同族动词，义为「闯入；打扰」
形容词加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「侵扰地」
形容词加后缀 -ness 构成，义为「侵扰性」

senses.title: Pushing into private matters
senses.definition: asking about or touching matters that belong to the private life of another person
senses.definitionCN: 打听或触碰属于别人私生活的事情
senses.example: The reporter asked an intrusive question about her marriage.
senses.exampleCN: 记者问了一个关于她婚姻的冒昧问题。
senses.why: The stem trud- means push, so the adjective describes a person or question that shoves into another private space.
senses.whyCN: 词干 trud- 意为「推」，所以这个形容词形容人或问题硬挤进别人的私人空间。

senses.title: Annoying in a sudden way
senses.definition: causing a sudden disturbance that interrupts what people are doing
senses.definitionCN: 突然造成干扰，打断人们正在做的事
senses.example: Popup windows are an intrusive part of the website.
senses.exampleCN: 弹窗是网站上扰人的一部分。
senses.why: An unwanted entry does not need to be personal to annoy people; a noise or notice that forces itself on you counts too.
senses.whyCN: 不受欢迎的进入不必涉及私事：一个强塞给人的声音或提示，同样算侵扰。

senses.title: Unwelcome in a place or system
senses.definition: entering or appearing in a place or system where it does not belong
senses.definitionCN: 进入或出现在本不属于它的地方或系统中
senses.example: Scientists studied several intrusive plant species.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家研究了几种外来入侵的植物物种。
senses.why: Physical entry against a barrier, extended to species, software, or devices, gives this wider sense.
senses.whyCN: 「顶着阻隔往里进」的物理画面推广到物种、软件或设备，就得到这个较宽的义项。

senses.title: Forced in from below as rock
senses.definition: describing rock that has been forced into existing rock layers in a molten state
senses.definitionCN: 描述熔融状态下挤入已有岩层的岩石
senses.example: The granite is an intrusive rock that cooled underground.
senses.exampleCN: 花岗岩是一种在地下冷却的侵入岩。
senses.why: Geology uses the same push-in idea for magma that forces its way between older strata.
senses.whyCN: 地质学用同样的「往里挤」概念，指岩浆强行进入更老的岩层之间。

senses.title: Of a speech sound between others
senses.definition: relating to an extra sound inserted between other sounds in speech
senses.definitionCN: 指说话时插在两个音之间的多余音
senses.example: Linguists describe the added consonant as intrusive.
senses.exampleCN: 语言学家把多出来的辅音称作增音。
senses.why: A sound slipping in between neighbours is a small, everyday version of the pushing-in image.
senses.whyCN: 一个音溜进相邻两音之间，是「往里挤」意象的小型日常版本。

intro.en: Intrusive is formed from Latin intrus-, the stem of intrudere, plus the English suffix -ive.
intro.cn: intrusive 由拉丁语 intrus-（intrudere 的词干）加上英语后缀 -ive 构成。

items.en: Trudere means to thrust or push.
items.cn: trudere 意为推、挤。

items.en: Intrudere means to push in or force in.
items.cn: intrudere 意为推入、强行进入。

items.en: The participle stem intrus- gives the English adjective.
items.cn: 分词词干 intrus- 提供英语形容词的词干。

items.en: Intrusive first appears as an adjective of a body pushing in.
items.cn: 英语中 intrusive 起初是形容词，描写「往里挤」的动作。

items.en: The word widens to geological rock that has been forced into others.
items.cn: 后来词义扩展到被挤入其他岩层的岩石。

items.en: Modern English applies it to privacy, advertising, and thoughts.
items.cn: 现代英语把它用于隐私、广告与念头等场景。

note.en: Intrusive is the adjective paired with intrude and intrusion, and close to meddling, prying, and obtrusive.
note.cn: intrusive 是与 intrude、intrusion 配对的形容词，近义区有 meddling、prying、obtrusive。

entries.definition: to enter where one is not wanted
an unwanted entry
a person who forces a way in
too obvious or noticeable, but with a different prefix
entries.definitionCN: 醒目的；爱出风头的；只是拼写相近，词源前缀不同

entries.definition: interfering in the affairs of others without being asked
entries.definitionCN: 好管闲事的；干涉他人的

entries.definition: asking about the private life of other people
forcing a will on others in a bossy way

normalIntro.en: Intrusive is the adjective inside the family intrude, intrusion, intruder; the ending -ive marks a quality.
normalIntro.cn: intrusive 是 intrude、intrusion、intruder 这一族词里的形容词，结尾 -ive 表示「带有某性质的」。

normal.en: Drop -de from intrude and add -ive to describe the quality of pushing in.
normal.cn: 把 intrude 的尾 -de 换成 -ive，就得到「爱往里挤的」这个性质形容词。

normal.en: Compare decisive and divisive: the same -sive ending marks a tendency.
normal.cn: 对比 decisive 与 divisive，同样的 -sive 结尾都表示某种倾向。

normal.en: Intrusive pairs with a thing that invades: an intrusive question, an intrusive ad.
normal.cn: intrusive 常修饰侵入之物：冒昧的问题、扰人的广告。

normal.en: In geology, intrusive rock cooled deep underground after being pushed into older layers.
normal.cn: 在地质学里，侵入岩是被挤入老岩层后在地下深处冷却形成的岩石。

normal.en: The adverb form intrusive + ly describes how someone acts.
normal.cn: 副词形式由 intrusive 加 -ly 构成，描写人做事的方式。

abstract.en: Picture a fingertip slipping into a drawer that belongs to someone else.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手尖伸进属于别人的抽屉。

abstract.en: Imagine a phone screen lighting up in the middle of a film you love.
abstract.cn: 想象在最爱的电影中间，手机屏幕突然亮起。

abstract.en: See dark granite fingers pressing up between pale layers of stone.
abstract.cn: 想象深色花岗岩的指状岩脉从浅色岩层之间向上顶出。

examples.en: Filming passengers without consent feels intrusive.
examples.cn: 未经同意拍摄乘客让人觉得很冒犯。

examples.en: The app was criticised for its intrusive tracking.
examples.cn: 这款应用因侵入式追踪而受到批评。

examples.en: An intrusive memory kept returning to the soldier.
examples.cn: 一段侵入性的记忆不断回到那名士兵脑中。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因戳西屋」——硬戳进西边那间屋，就是「侵入的」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（向里）+ trudere（推）→ intrudere（推入）→ 词干 intrus- + 后缀 -ive → 英语 intrusive，核心义「爱往里挤的」。

sensesIntro.en: Intrusive starts with people or questions entering private space, then covers any unwelcome disturbance, entry, rock, and sound.
sensesIntro.cn: intrusive 先从人或问题闯进私人空间开始，再覆盖一切不受欢迎的干扰、进入、岩石与语音。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fingertip poking into another person drawer.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根指尖戳进别人的抽屉。

branches.en: The quality of prying into private matters is the first sense.
branches.cn: 刺探私事的性质是第一义项。

branches.en: Any sudden annoyance repeats the quality in daily life.
branches.cn: 任何突然的烦扰在日常生活中重复这一性质。

branches.en: Things that do not belong somewhere are called intrusive too.
branches.cn: 不属于某处的事物同样被称为侵入的。

branches.en: Rock forced between layers keeps the physical image in geology.
branches.cn: 被挤入岩层之间的岩石在地质学中保留物理意象。

branches.en: An extra speech sound is a tiny forced entry between neighbours.
branches.cn: 多余的语音是两音之间的一次微小强行进入。

intro.en: Intrusive joins the Latin stem intrus- to the English suffix -ive, which marks a quality or tendency.
intro.cn: intrusive 把拉丁词干 intrus- 与英语后缀 -ive 结合，-ive 表示性质或倾向。

latinIntro.en: Latin in- means in or into and trudere means to push, giving intrudere, to push in.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 in- 意为「向内」，trudere 意为「推」，合成 intrudere（推入）。

items.example: The prefix in- points the action inward.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 把动作指向内部。

items.example: Trudere gives the family its pushing stem.
items.exampleCN: trudere 为整族词提供「推」的词干。

items.example: Intrudere is the source of the English family.
items.exampleCN: intrudere 是英语这一族词的来源。

items.meaningCN: 表示具有某倾向的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ive forms the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ive 构成形容词。

items.example: The stem intrus- links verb and adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词干 intrus- 连接动词与形容词。

items.example: Intrusive also describes magma rock.
items.exampleCN: intrusive 也用来形容岩浆岩。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms intrusively.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 intrusively。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms intrusiveness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 intrusiveness。

items.example: Intrusion is the matching noun.
items.exampleCN: intrusion 是与之配对的名词。

items.example: Compare protrude, which pushes forward.
items.exampleCN: 对比 protrude，意为向前推出。

definition_zh: 直觉；直觉力；直觉产生的想法；洞察力
definition_en: the ability to know or understand something at once, without conscious reasoning or proof
core_image: 还没有推理，答案先在心中亮起，像有人在耳边低声说出
scene: 老医生说不出理由，却一看到病人就断定情况不对，后来的化验证实了。Her intuition said that something was wrong even before the test results came back.
sceneCN: 这里 intuition 是「直觉」（第 1 个义项：不经推理便知道某事的能力），句意：老医生凭直觉发现病人情况不对，化验随后证实。

derivatives.zh: 加后缀 -ive 构成，义为「凭直觉的；易懂的」
反向构词，义为「凭直觉知道」
加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「凭直觉地」
加后缀 -ally 构成的罕见副词，义为「凭直觉地」

senses.title: Knowing without reasoning
senses.definition: the power of understanding or deciding something directly, without step by step reasoning
senses.definitionCN: 不经过一步步推理就能直接理解或判断的能力
senses.example: Her intuition warned her that the deal was wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 她的直觉告诉这笔交易有问题。
senses.why: Latin in- means on or at and tueri means to look, so the core image is a steady inner look that answers before reasoning does.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 in- 意为「在」，tueri 意为「看」，核心意象是内心一次专注的注视，在推理之前就给出答案。

senses.title: An immediate inner certainty
senses.definition: an idea or feeling that appears suddenly and feels certain without proof
senses.definitionCN: 突然出现、无需证据便让人确信的想法或感觉
senses.example: My first intuition was that he was lying.
senses.exampleCN: 我的第一直觉是他在说谎。
senses.why: Once the inner look delivers an answer, that answer is named by the same word.
senses.whyCN: 内心的注视一旦给出答案，这个答案也就用同一个词来称呼。

senses.title: Insight into falsehood
senses.definition: a sharp awareness of what is true or false, especially in people and situations
senses.definitionCN: 对人对事的真假特别敏锐的觉察
senses.example: The detective has a remarkable intuition about people.
senses.exampleCN: 这位侦探对人有非凡的洞察力。
senses.why: Trained inner looking becomes a reliable talent, so the same noun can name personal insight.
senses.whyCN: 经过训练的「内看」会成为可靠的天赋，于是这个词也能指个人的洞察力。

senses.title: Direct awareness taught by philosophy
senses.definition: immediate awareness of a truth of reason, apart from sense experience or deduction
senses.definitionCN: 不依赖感官经验或演绎，对理性真理的直接领悟
senses.example: Kant treats space as given through intuition.
senses.exampleCN: 康德把空间视为通过直观给出的东西。
senses.why: Philosophy fixes the old inner-look image into a technical term for direct cognition.
senses.whyCN: 哲学把这个「内看」的旧意象固定为指直接认识的术语。

senses.title: A felt sense that guides action
senses.definition: a vague but strong feeling that steers a choice or warns of danger
senses.definitionCN: 虽模糊却强烈的感觉，引导选择或预示危险
senses.example: She ignored her intuition and took the night train.
senses.exampleCN: 她没理会自己的预感，坐上了夜车。
senses.why: The inner voice that looks ahead turns into a wordless warning that sets the body moving.
senses.whyCN: 那种向前的内视变成没有语言的警告，推动身体行动，于是这个词也指预感。

intro.en: Intuition comes from Late Latin intuitio, a looking at, from intueri, to look on or regard attentively.
intro.cn: intuition 来自晚期拉丁语 intuitio（注视），源于 intueri（看着、留意）。

items.en: Tueri means to look at or watch over.
items.cn: tueri 意为看、注视、守护。

items.en: In- adds the sense of on or at to tueri.
items.cn: in- 在 tueri 前加上「在……之上／朝……看」之意。

items.en: Intueri means to look on or regard, and intuitio means a looking at.
items.cn: intueri 意为注视、留意，intuitio 意为一次注视。

items.en: Scholastic writers used intuitio for direct mental vision.
items.cn: 经院哲学家用 intuitio 指心灵对事物的直接看见。

items.en: The learned word enters French and then English in the same century.
items.cn: 这个学术词先进入法语，随后在同世纪进入英语。

items.en: Modern English turns the looking inward into the common sense of instant knowing.
items.cn: 现代英语把「看」转向内部，形成今天「瞬间知道」的常用义。

note.en: Intuition belongs with the adjective intuitive and the verb intuit, and shares its field with instinct, hunch, and insight.
note.cn: intuition 与形容词 intuitive、反向构词动词 intuit 同族，近义区有 instinct、hunch、insight。

entries.definition: based on feeling rather than reasoning
to know by feeling rather than proof
by way of direct feeling
the quality of being easy to grasp at once
a natural impulse that needs no reasoning
a vague feeling that something will happen
a clear understanding of a complex problem

normalIntro.en: Intuition is a Latin look turned inward: intueri, to look at, plus the noun ending -ion.
normalIntro.cn: intuition 是一个被转向内部的「看」：intueri（注视）加上名词后缀 -ion。

normal.en: The -tion ending marks a noun of action, as in attention and intention.
normal.cn: 结尾 -tion 标记动作名词，如 attention 与 intention。

normal.en: The stem tue- means look, so intuition is a steady inner look.
normal.cn: 词干 tue- 意为「看」，所以 intuition 是一次专注的内看。

normal.en: Intuition pairs with the adjective intuitive and the back-formed verb intuit.
normal.cn: intuition 与形容词 intuitive 及反向构成的动词 intuit 配对。

normal.en: Trust your intuition is one of the most common phrases with the word.
normal.cn: trust your intuition 是这个词最常见的说法之一。

normal.en: People often say a flash of intuition to mean a sudden inner answer.
normal.cn: 人们常说 a flash of intuition，指一闪而过的内心答案。

abstract.en: See a dim lamp switch on inside your head before you explain why.
abstract.cn: 想象你还没法解释原因，脑中一盏小灯先亮了。

abstract.en: Imagine a doctor glancing at a patient and stopping short.
abstract.cn: 想象一名医生扫了病人一眼就立刻停住脚步。

abstract.en: Picture a compass needle swinging to north before you check the map.
abstract.cn: 想象你还没查地图，指南针已经指向北方。

examples.en: You should trust your intuition when you meet strangers.
examples.cn: 碰到陌生人时，你应当相信自己的直觉。

examples.en: His intuition about the market proved right.
examples.cn: 他对市场的直觉被证明是对的。

examples.en: She never ignores a warning from intuition.
examples.cn: 她从不忽视直觉给出的警告。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因推神」——下意识里那股神推了你一把，就是直觉；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（在内）+ tueri（看）→ intueri（注视）→ 晚期拉丁语 intuitio（注视）→ 法语 → 英语 intuition，核心义「向内看，一眼看穿」。

sensesIntro.en: Intuition starts as a steady inward look, then names the sudden answer, the sharp insight, the philosophical term, and the warning feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: intuition 从专注的「向内看」出发，接着指突然给出的答案、敏锐的洞察、哲学术语，以及预警的感觉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp that lights up inside the head before any explanation.
core.cn: 核心意象：还没来得及解释，脑中先亮起一盏灯。

branches.en: The power of knowing without reasoning is the first sense.
branches.cn: 不经推理便知的能力是第一义项。

branches.en: The sudden answer that the inner look produces is named next.
branches.cn: 内看所产出的突然答案紧接其后。

branches.en: A trained inward look becomes practical insight.
branches.cn: 训练有素的内看成为实际的洞察力。

branches.en: Philosophy fixes direct cognition as a technical term.
branches.cn: 哲学把直接认知固定为专门术语。

branches.en: The look ahead becomes a wordless warning feeling.
branches.cn: 向前方的注视变成没有语言的预警感觉。

intro.en: Intuition is built from Latin in- plus tueri, and gathers intuitive, intuit, and the noun ending -tion.
intro.cn: intuition 由拉丁语 in- 与 tueri 构成，并聚拢 intuitive、intuit 与名词后缀 -tion。

latinIntro.en: Latin in- means in or on and tueri means to look at, so intueri means to look on or regard.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 in- 意为「在……之内／之上」，tueri 意为「看」，因此 intueri 意为注视、留意。

items.example: The prefix in- turns the gaze inward.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 把视线转向内部。

items.example: Tueri gives the family its looking stem.
items.exampleCN: tueri 为这一族词提供「看」的词干。

items.example: Intueri is the direct source of intuition.
items.exampleCN: intueri 是 intuition 的直接来源。

items.example: Intuition is the noun of the family.
items.exampleCN: intuition 是这一族的中心名词。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或过程的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -tion makes a noun of action.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -tion 构成动作名词。

items.meaning: reached by feeling, easy to grasp
items.example: Intuitive describes a person or a design.
items.exampleCN: intuitive 可形容人或设计。

items.meaningCN: 表示具有某性质的形容词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ive forms intuitive.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ive 构成 intuitive。

items.example: Intuit is a back-formation from intuition.
items.exampleCN: intuit 是从 intuition 反向构成的动词。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms intuitively.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 intuitively。

definition_zh: 淹没；泛滥；使不堪承受；大量涌入
definition_en: to cover an area with a flood of water, or to give or send someone far more of something than they can deal with
core_image: 河水漫过堤岸，把整片平地吞进水里
scene: 暴雨过后，河水漫过堤岸，淹没了整座村庄。After the heavy rain, the river broke its banks and began to inundate the whole village.
sceneCN: 这里 inundate 是「淹没、泛滥」（第 1 个义项：水流漫过并覆盖某地）；句意：暴雨过后，河水冲垮堤岸，开始淹没整个村庄。

pos.zh: 使应接不暇；使不堪承受

collocations.zh: 被……淹没；收到大量……而不堪承受

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「水灾；淹没；洪水般的涌入」
过去分词转形容词，义为「被淹没的；被大量事物压垮的」
现在分词转形容词，义为「铺天盖地而来的；倾泻的」

senses.title: To cover land with flood water
senses.definition: to cover a place with water that has overflowed its normal limits
senses.definitionCN: 让溢出正常界限的水覆盖某个地方
senses.example: Heavy rain inundated the low-lying fields.
senses.exampleCN: 大雨淹没了低洼的田地。
senses.why: Latin in- here means on or upon, and unda means a wave, so the word pictures water breaking in on land as a wave.
senses.whyCN: 这里的拉丁语前缀 in- 表示「在……之上」，unda 意为「波浪」，所以这个词的画面是水像浪头一样扑上陆地。

senses.title: To overwhelm someone with too much
senses.titleCN: 使应接不暇；使不堪承受
senses.definition: to give or send someone so many things that they cannot deal with them all
senses.definitionCN: 给某人或向某人发送过多事物，以致对方无法应付
senses.example: After the broadcast, the office was inundated with calls.
senses.exampleCN: 节目播出后，办公室被电话淹没了。
senses.why: If water can drown a field, then letters, calls, or requests can drown a person in the same way.
senses.whyCN: 既然水能淹没田地，那么信件、电话或请求也能用同样的方式把人淹没。

senses.title: To flood a market or system
senses.definition: to cause a very large number of goods or people to enter a place at once
senses.definitionCN: 使大量商品或人同时进入某地
senses.example: Cheap imports have inundated the local market.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价进口货大量涌入了本地市场。
senses.why: The flooding image extends to commerce, where a sudden mass of goods flows into a market like water.
senses.whyCN: 「淹没」的画面延伸到商业领域：突然大量涌入的商品就像流进市场的水。

intro.en: Inundate comes from Latin inundare, from in- onto and unda, a wave; it entered English in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: inundate 来自拉丁语 inundare，由 in-（在……之上）与 unda（波浪）构成，十六世纪进入英语。

items.en: Unda means a wave or a rush of water.
items.cn: unda 意为波浪、水的奔涌。

items.en: Inundare means to overflow, flood, or submerge land.
items.cn: inundare 意为溢出、泛滥、淹没陆地。

items.en: Inundatio names a flood or an overflow.
items.cn: inundatio 指洪水、泛滥。

items.en: The verb inundate enters English as a word of rivers and floods.
items.cn: 动词 inundate 作为写河流与洪水的词进入英语。

items.en: Inundated with letters and requests begins to describe people, not only land.
items.cn: inundated with 开始用于描述人（被信件、请求淹没），而不再只用于土地。

items.en: Inundate now describes email, orders, and markets as well as water.
items.cn: 现代英语中，inundate 除了水，还用来描述邮件、订单与市场。

note.en: Inundate shares the Latin wave root unda with abundant and undulate, and stays formal next to everyday flood.
note.cn: inundate 与 abundant、undulate 共享拉丁语「波浪」词根 unda，比日常词 flood 更正式。

entries.definition: a flood or an overwhelming mass of things
existing in large quantities
entries.definitionCN: 大量存在的；丰富的；出自同一拉丁语波浪词根 unda

entries.definition: to move in a wave-like motion
entries.definitionCN: 起伏；波动；同出 unda（波浪）

entries.definition: to cover an area with a large amount of water
entries.definitionCN: 淹没；泛滥（日常词，比 inundate 常用）

entries.definition: a great flood, or to overwhelm with a mass of things
entries.definitionCN: 洪水；倾泻；淹没（语气比 inundate 更强）

entries.definition: to put or go completely under water

normalIntro.en: Inundate is Latin in- onto plus unda wave, so remember the wave that comes on shore.
normalIntro.cn: inundate 是拉丁语 in-（在……之上）加 unda（波浪），就记住那个扑上岸的浪。

normal.en: The root unda means wave, as in undulate, to move like waves.
normal.cn: 词根 unda 意为波浪，undulate（起伏）也用这个根。

normal.en: Be inundated with mail means to receive far too much mail.
normal.cn: be inundated with mail 指收到多得应付不来的邮件。

normal.en: The verb is transitive: water inundates land, requests inundate people.
normal.cn: 这是及物动词：水淹没土地，请求淹没某人。

normal.en: Compare flood for everyday speech and inundate for a formal or written tone.
normal.cn: 对比 flood（口语常用）与 inundate（书面、正式）。

normal.en: The noun is inundation, and the past participle inundated also works as an adjective.
normal.cn: 名词是 inundation，过去分词 inundated 也作形容词用。

abstract.en: Picture a swollen river climbing over the bank and sliding across a field.
abstract.cn: 想象一条涨满的河爬过河岸，顺着田地漫开。

abstract.en: Imagine an office buried under a mountain of letters.
abstract.cn: 想象一个办公室被一座信山埋住。

abstract.en: Picture a harbour gate opening and a wall of goods pouring in.
abstract.cn: 想象港口的闸门打开，一堵商品墙涌了进来。

examples.en: The storm surge inundated the coastal roads.
examples.cn: 风暴潮淹没了沿海公路。

examples.en: Since the review appeared, the restaurant has been inundated with bookings.
examples.cn: 自从那篇评论发表，这家餐厅的订位就多得应接不暇。

examples.en: Local shops were inundated with orders before the holiday.
examples.cn: 节日前，当地商店被大量订单淹没。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因淹的」——水「因」为太多而「淹」了地，就是用 inundate 表达淹没；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（在……之上）+ unda（波浪）→ inundare（泛滥、淹没）→ 英语 inundate，核心义「水像浪一样漫上来」。

sensesIntro.en: Inundate starts with water covering land, then extends to people overwhelmed by messages, and finally to goods pouring into a market.
sensesIntro.cn: inundate 先从水漫过土地讲起，再延伸到人被大量消息压垮，最后指商品涌入市场。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a river climbing its bank and swallowing the flat land.
core.cn: 核心意象：河水爬过河岸，吞没整片平地。

branches.en: The literal flood covering land is the base sense.
branches.cn: 字面意义上水漫过土地是最基本的义项。

branches.en: The overwhelming sense grows from the idea of drowning.
branches.cn: 「被压垮」的义项衍生于「被淹没」这一比喻。

branches.en: Goods pouring into a market keep the image of a great inflow.
branches.cn: 商品涌入市场保留了「大量流进」的画面。

branches.en: Both land and people can be inundated with something.
branches.cn: 土地与人都会 be inundated with 某物。

branches.en: Too many emails and too much stock share the sense of an unstoppable tide.
branches.cn: 过多的邮件与过多的库存都带着「挡不住的潮水」意味。

intro.en: Inundate is built from the Latin prefix in- and the noun root unda, a wave.
intro.cn: inundate 由拉丁语前缀 in- 与名词词根 unda（波浪）构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin in- means onto or upon, and unda means a wave; the two give the idea of a wave breaking onto land.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 in- 意为在……之上，unda 意为波浪；两者合起来就是浪头扑上陆地。

items.example: The prefix in- places the wave onto the land.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 把波浪放到土地之上。

items.example: Unda gives the core image of the wave.
items.exampleCN: unda 提供「波浪」这一核心意象。

items.example: Inundare is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: inundare 是直接拉丁语来源。

items.example: Inundate keeps the flooding sense.
items.exampleCN: inundate 保留了「淹没」的含义。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或状态的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ation forms inundation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成 inundation。

items.example: Inundation names the flood itself.
items.exampleCN: inundation 指洪水本身。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms inundated.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 inundated。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms inundating.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 inundating。

items.example: Undulate shows the same wave root.
items.exampleCN: undulate 显示同一个波浪词根。

items.example: Abundant also comes from unda, through overflowing water.
items.exampleCN: abundant 也来自 unda，经由「水溢出」引申为「丰富」。

definition_zh: 入侵者；侵略者；侵入物种
definition_en: a person, army, or other group that enters a country or place by force in order to take control of it
core_image: 一队士兵踏过边境，闯进别人的家园
scene: 村口的人敲响警钟，因为远方的入侵者已经越过山岭。The villagers rang the alarm bell because the invaders had already crossed the hills.
sceneCN: 这里 invaders 是「入侵者、侵略者」（第 1 个义项：以武力闯入他国的人或军队）；句意：村民们敲响了警报钟，因为入侵者已经翻过了山岭。

derivatives.zh: 基础动词，义为「侵入；侵略；侵犯」
由动词加 -sion 构成，义为「侵入；侵略；侵犯」
由动词加 -ive 构成，义为「侵入性的；扩散的；入侵的」
现在分词转形容词，义为「入侵的；侵入的」

senses.title: A person or army that enters by force
senses.definition: a person, group, or army that enters a place in order to take it over
senses.definitionCN: 为夺取某地而闯入其中的个人、团体或军队
senses.example: The invaders reached the river within a week.
senses.exampleCN: 入侵者一周内就抵达了河边。
senses.why: The Latin verb invadere means to go into, and its prefix in- pushes the action inward against a boundary.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 invadere 意为「走进去」，前缀 in- 把动作向内推，越过边界。

senses.title: A species spreading into new ground
senses.definition: an animal or plant that spreads into an area where it did not live before and harms local life
senses.definitionCN: 扩散到原先并不栖息的地区并危害当地生物的动植物
senses.example: The river is now home to several invaders from other regions.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河里如今有好几种来自其他地区的入侵物种。
senses.why: The same idea of entering and taking space is applied to plants and animals that crowd out native life.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「闯入并占据空间」概念被用在挤走本地生物的动植物身上。

senses.title: Someone who intrudes on private space
senses.definition: a person who intrudes where he or she is not wanted, often into private matters
senses.definitionCN: 闯进不该进之处或干涉私事的人
senses.example: She treats any question about her salary as an invader of her privacy.
senses.exampleCN: 她把任何询问薪水的说法都看作对自己隐私的侵犯。
senses.why: In everyday use the boundary can be personal space rather than a border, so the intruder becomes an invader of privacy.
senses.whyCN: 在日常用法里，被越过的边界可以是私人空间而非国界，闯入者就成了侵犯隐私的人。

intro.en: Invader comes from Latin invadere, to go into or attack, built from in- in and vadere to go.
intro.cn: invader 来自拉丁语 invadere（走进去、进攻），由 in-（进入）与 vadere（走）构成。

items.en: Vadere is an old Latin verb meaning to go or to proceed.
items.cn: vadere 是古拉丁语动词，意为走、行进。

items.en: In- adds the direction in, giving invadere, to go into or attack.
items.cn: in- 加上「向内」的方向，构成 invadere，意为走进去、进攻。

items.en: Invadere develops the military sense of entering an enemy land.
items.cn: invadere 发展出进入敌国领土的军事含义。

items.en: Old French envair gives English the verb invade.
items.cn: 古法语 envair 给英语带来动词 invade。

items.en: Invader enters English as a name for an enemy that marches in.
items.cn: invader 作为「闯进来的敌人」进入英语。

items.en: Ecology borrows the word for invasive species and their spread.
items.cn: 二十世纪生态学借用该词描述入侵物种及其扩散。

note.en: Invader belongs to the Latin vadere family with invade, invasion, and invasive, and sits close to intruder and attacker.
note.cn: invader 属于拉丁语 vadere 词族，与 invade、invasion、invasive 同源，与 intruder、attacker 意义相邻。

entries.definition: to enter a place by force
the act of entering by force
spreading where it is not wanted
entries.definitionCN: 侵入性的；入侵的；扩散的

entries.definition: a person who enters a place where they are not allowed
entries.definitionCN: 闯入者；不速之客（多指私人场所）

entries.definition: a person who attacks
a person or army that controls a place by force

normalIntro.en: Invader is the person form of invade: entering inward by force.
normalIntro.cn: invader 是 invade 的人形：向内强行进入的人。

normal.en: The suffix -er turns invade into the name of the one who does it.
normal.cn: 后缀 -er 把 invade 变成「做这个动作的人」。

normal.en: Invade and invasion use the Latin vadere, to go.
normal.cn: invade 与 invasion 都用了拉丁语 vadere（走）。

normal.en: Repel the invaders is a common news phrase about defence.
normal.cn: repel the invaders 是新闻里谈防御的常见说法。

normal.en: In science, an invader can be a plant or animal, not only an army.
normal.cn: 在科学语境里，invader 也可以是动植物，而不只是军队。

normal.en: Compare intruder: an intruder breaks into a private place, an invader takes a whole country.
normal.cn: 对比 intruder：intruder 闯进私人场所，invader 占领整个国家。

abstract.en: Picture boots crossing a border line in the dust.
abstract.cn: 想象靴子踏过尘土里的边界线。

abstract.en: Picture a foreign weed climbing over a garden wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵外来杂草翻过花园的墙。

abstract.en: Picture a stranger walking uninvited into a private room.
abstract.cn: 想象一个陌生人未经允许走进私人房间。

examples.en: The castle held out against the invaders for three months.
examples.cn: 城堡抵御入侵者坚守了三个月。

examples.en: Biologists track how fast the invader spreads through the lake.
examples.cn: 生物学家追踪这种入侵物种在湖中扩散的速度。

examples.en: The invaders burned most of the harbour before they left.
examples.cn: 入侵者在离开前烧毁了港口的大部分。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一喂的」——闯进你家还要你「一喂」到底的，就是 invader；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（进入）+ vadere（走）→ invadere（走进、进攻）→ invade → invader，核心义「越过边界走进去的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Invader starts as the person who enters by force, then shifts to species that spread into new ground, and finally to anyone who crosses a private boundary.
sensesIntro.cn: invader 先指以武力闯入的人，再转指扩散到新地区的物种，最后指跨越私人边界的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: soldiers stepping across a border toward a village.
core.cn: 核心意象：士兵越过边境，朝村庄走去。

branches.en: The military invader is the central sense.
branches.cn: 军事意义上的入侵者是核心义项。

branches.en: Species entering new ground reuse the same image.
branches.cn: 进入新地域的物种沿用了同一个画面。

branches.en: An intruder on personal space is the everyday extension.
branches.cn: 侵扰私人空间的人是日常用法的延伸。

branches.en: Armies and alien species both arrive from somewhere else.
branches.cn: 军队与外来物种都是从别处闯进来的。

branches.en: Both senses lean on the idea of an unwanted guest.
branches.cn: 两个义项都依赖「不受欢迎的闯入者」这一想法。

intro.en: Invader joins the Latin prefix in- to the verb root vadere, then adds the English agent suffix -er.
intro.cn: invader 把拉丁语前缀 in- 与动词词根 vadere 相连，再加英语施动后缀 -er。

latinIntro.en: Latin in- means into, vadere means to go, and invadere means to go into or attack.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 in- 意为进入，vadere 意为走，invadere 意为走进去、进攻。

items.example: The prefix in- points the going inward.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 把「走」的方向指向内部。

items.example: Vadere supplies the motion of going.
items.exampleCN: vadere 提供「走」的动作。

items.example: Invadere is the direct source of invade.
items.exampleCN: invadere 是 invade 的直接来源。

items.example: Invade is the English verb.
items.exampleCN: invade 是英语动词。

items.example: The suffix -er forms invader.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 invader。

items.example: The suffix -sion forms invasion.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -sion 构成 invasion。

items.meaningCN: 表示性质的形容词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ive forms invasive.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ive 构成 invasive。

items.example: Invasion names the act itself.
items.exampleCN: invasion 指入侵这一行为本身。

items.example: Invasive describes species that spread fast.
items.exampleCN: invasive 描述扩散迅速的物种。

items.example: Evade uses the same vadere root with the prefix e-.
items.exampleCN: evade 用同一个 vadere 词根，配前缀 e-。

definition_zh: 无效的；站不住脚的；病人；残疾人
definition_en: not legally or officially acceptable, or not reasonable and based on correct thinking; as a noun, a person who is ill or disabled and needs care
core_image: 一张盖了章却被红线划掉的票据：看着像真的，其实不成立
scene: 检票员在车门口拦下乘客，说那张过期的车票已经无效。At the gate the inspector stopped the passenger and said the expired ticket was invalid.
sceneCN: 这里 invalid 是「无效的、不合法的」（第 1 个义项：不被官方承认、失去效力）；句意：检票员在车门口拦下乘客，说那张过期的车票已经无效。

pos.zh: 无效的；不合法的；站不住脚的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加 -ity 构成，义为「无效性；无法律效力」
同根词，义为「确认有效；验证」
加否定前缀 in- 之前的原词，义为「有效的；正当的」
复合名词，义为「病残补助金」

senses.title: Not legally or officially acceptable
senses.definition: not accepted by law or by an official body, and therefore without effect
senses.definitionCN: 不被法律或官方机构接受，因而没有效力
senses.example: The old passport is now invalid.
senses.exampleCN: 这本旧护照现在已失效。
senses.why: The prefix in- negates the Latin adjective validus, strong or effective, so an invalid document has no force behind it.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 in- 否定了拉丁语形容词 validus（强壮、有效），所以 invalid 的文件在法理上没有力量。

senses.title: Not based on sound reasoning
senses.definition: not well reasoned or based on facts, so it does not hold up
senses.definitionCN: 推理或事实依据不足，因而经不起推敲
senses.example: His conclusion rests on an invalid comparison.
senses.exampleCN: 他的结论建立在一个不成立的比较之上。
senses.why: If a document loses legal force, a line of reasoning can lose logical force in the same way.
senses.whyCN: 既然文件会失去法律效力，一条推理也可以以同样方式失去逻辑效力。

senses.title: A person who is ill or disabled
senses.definition: a person weakened by illness or disability who needs care
senses.definitionCN: 因病或残疾而虚弱、需要照顾的人
senses.example: The crutches once marked an invalid for life.
senses.exampleCN: 拐杖过去意味着一个人终身是个病人。
senses.why: This noun goes back through French to Latin invalidus, not strong, so it describes a person without bodily strength.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词经由法语追溯到拉丁语 invalidus（不强壮），指一个身体没有力气的人。

intro.en: Invalid combines the Latin prefix in-, meaning not, with validus, strong, from valere, to be strong; the two senses took separate paths through French.
intro.cn: invalid 由拉丁语否定前缀 in- 与 validus（强壮的，源于 valere「强壮」）构成；两个义项经由法语走了不同的路。

items.en: Valere means to be strong, to be well, or to be worth something.
items.cn: valere 意为强壮、健康或有价值。

items.en: Validus means strong and effective, and invalidus means not strong.
items.cn: validus 意为强壮、有效的，invalidus 意为不强壮的。

items.en: French invalide first describes a person weakened by illness.
items.cn: 十六世纪法语 invalide 最初描述因病而虚弱的人。

items.en: The noun invalid names a soldier unfit for duty and then any sick person.
items.cn: 名词 invalid 先指不能服兵役的士兵，后泛指病人。

items.en: The adjective develops the legal sense of having no force.
items.cn: 形容词发展出「没有法律效力」的含义。

items.en: Modern use adds invalid data in computing and the adjective invalid for arguments.
items.cn: 现代用法增添了计算机里的「无效数据」以及形容论点不成立的用法。

note.en: Invalid is the negative of valid, and its family includes validate, validity, and the noun form for a sick person.
note.cn: invalid 是 valid 的否定形式，词族包括 validate、validity，另有「病人」这一名词义。

entries.definition: legally acceptable or well reasoned
entries.definitionCN: 有效的；正当的；成立的反义词原形

entries.definition: to prove or confirm that something is acceptable
the state of being invalid
having no legal force, as of a contract
having no legal or binding force
having no purpose or sense

normalIntro.en: Invalid is simply in- not plus valid: the document or the argument has no force.
normalIntro.cn: invalid 就是 in-（不）加 valid（有效）：文件或论证都没有效力。

normal.en: Valid comes from Latin valere, to be strong, so invalid means not strong.
normal.cn: valid 来自拉丁语 valere（强壮），所以 invalid 意为「不强、无效」。

normal.en: In everyday use invalid pairs with expired or declared.
normal.cn: 日常说法常配 expired 或 declared，如车票失效、被宣布无效。

normal.en: The verb is invalidate, and the noun is invalidity.
normal.cn: 动词是 invalidate，名词是 invalidity。

normal.en: As a noun, the pronunciation /ˈɪnvəlɪd/ links to invalidus, not strong in body.
normal.cn: 作名词时读音为 /ˈɪnvəlɪd/，联系到 invalidus（身体不强壮）。

normal.en: Compare void and null for contracts, and sound or valid for reasoning.
normal.cn: 合同多用 void、null；论证则用 valid 或 sound 描述。

abstract.en: Picture a stamped ticket with a red line drawn across it.
abstract.cn: 想象一张盖了章的车票上被画了一条红线。

abstract.en: Picture a chain of blocks collapsing at the missing link.
abstract.cn: 想象一串积木在缺环处塌掉。

abstract.en: Modern English: setting something to invalid means the field will not be saved.
abstract.cn: 现代英语中，把某项设为 invalid 意味着该字段不会被保存。

examples.en: Your warranty becomes invalid once the seal is broken.
examples.cn: 一旦拆封，你的保修就失效了。

examples.en: The court ruled that the contract was invalid.
examples.cn: 法庭裁定该合同无效。

examples.en: That argument is invalid because it ignores the counterexample.
examples.cn: 那个论点站不住脚，因为它忽略了反例。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因外来」——外来的票据「因」为不是本店的而「无效」，正好对上 invalid 的「无效」义；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ validus（强壮的）← valere（强壮、有价值）→ 法语 invalide → 英语 invalid，核心义「没有力量的」。

sensesIntro.en: Invalid begins with legal force being denied, moves to reasoning that does not hold, and ends with the old noun for a person without bodily strength.
sensesIntro.cn: invalid 从「被剥夺法律效力」讲起，转到「推理不成立」，最后是老名词义「身体不强壮的人」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stamped paper cut through by a red line.
core.cn: 核心意象：盖了章的纸被一道红线划掉。

branches.en: No legal force is the main modern sense.
branches.cn: 「无法律效力」是现代最主要的义项。

branches.en: A claim without logical force follows the same image.
branches.cn: 没有逻辑效力的论点沿用同一个画面。

branches.en: The noun for a sick person keeps the older meaning of weak.
branches.cn: 指病人的名词义保留了较早的「虚弱」含义。

branches.en: Contracts and arguments can both be struck down.
branches.cn: 合同和论证都可以被判定不成立。

branches.en: Both senses grew from Latin invalidus, not strong.
branches.cn: 两个义项都从拉丁语 invalidus（不强壮）生长出来。

intro.en: Invalid is the negative prefix in- on valid, which comes from Latin valere, to be strong.
intro.cn: invalid 是在 valid 前加否定前缀 in-，valid 来自拉丁语 valere（强壮）。

latinIntro.en: Latin valere means to be strong, and validus means strong or effective; in- turns it into its opposite.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 valere 意为强壮，validus 意为强壮、有效；in- 把它变成反面。

items.example: The prefix in- negates valid.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 否定 valid。

items.meaning: to be strong, to be worth
items.example: Valere gives the idea of strength.
items.exampleCN: valere 提供「力量」这一概念。

items.example: Validus is the direct adjective root.
items.exampleCN: validus 是直接形容词词根。

items.example: Valid is the positive form.
items.exampleCN: valid 是肯定形式。

items.example: The suffix -ate forms validate.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 构成 validate。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms validity.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 构成 validity。

items.example: Validate is the verb of making valid.
items.exampleCN: validate 是表示「使有效、验证」的动词。

items.example: Validity names the quality itself.
items.exampleCN: validity 指有效性这一属性本身。

items.example: Invalidate adds in- to validate.
items.exampleCN: invalidate 是在 validate 前加 in-。

items.example: Invalidity is the noun form of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: invalidity 是该形容词的名词形式。

definition_zh: 极宝贵的；无价的；无法估量的；不可或缺的
definition_en: extremely valuable, so useful or precious that its worth cannot be measured
core_image: 一件宝物流光溢彩，任何价签都无法标出它的价值
scene: 救援队捡回那本被水泡过的旧相册，里面装着祖父母的黑白照片。The flooded folder held only one item the rescue team called invaluable: a soaked album of family photos.
sceneCN: 这里 invaluable 是「极宝贵的、无价的」（第 1 个义项：价值高到无法衡量）；句意：救援队把所有物品逐一清点，唯独把一本被水浸透的家庭相册称为「无价之宝」。

pos.zh: 极宝贵的；无价的；无法估价的

derivatives.zh: 极宝贵地；无可估量地，由 invaluable 加 -ly 构成
有价值的；贵重的，去掉否定前缀 in- 后的肯定形式
价值；价格，词根词，动词义为「重视、评价」
无价值的；一文不值的，与 invaluable 意思完全相反

senses.title: Worth far more than any price
senses.definition: so precious or useful that no price could ever be put on it
senses.definitionCN: 珍贵或有用到根本无法标价的程度
senses.example: Her old letters are invaluable to the family.
senses.exampleCN: 她的旧信件对这家人来说是无价之宝。
senses.why: The prefix in- here means not, but the negation falls on the act of valuing, not on the worth of the thing.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 in- 表示「不」，但它否定的是「估价」这个动作，而不是物品本身的价值。

senses.title: Extremely useful in practice
senses.definition: extremely helpful to a person, plan, or activity
senses.definitionCN: 对某人、某项计划或活动极有帮助
senses.example: Local knowledge proved invaluable during the survey.
senses.exampleCN: 在勘察过程中，当地人的了解被证明极为有用。
senses.why: What cannot be priced is often what you cannot do without, so the word slides from worth to usefulness.
senses.whyCN: 无法标价的东西往往也是你离不开的东西，于是词义从「珍贵」滑向「极其有用」。

senses.title: A resource that cannot be replaced
senses.definition: a contribution, skill, or record that is impossible to replace once lost
senses.definitionCN: 一旦失去便无法替代的贡献、技艺或记录
senses.example: Her knowledge of the archive proved invaluable to the team.
senses.exampleCN: 她对档案库的了解对团队来说不可或缺。
senses.why: Since its value escapes all accounting, such a resource sits outside any budget and cannot be bought back.
senses.whyCN: 正因为它的价值无法核算，这类资源游离在任何预算之外，一旦失去就买不回来。

senses.title: Gratitude for rare help
senses.definition: used to praise help, advice, or experience whose worth is not measured by money
senses.definitionCN: 用来称赞帮助、建议或经验，其价值不以金钱衡量
senses.example: I owe you invaluable advice on my first year.
senses.exampleCN: 第一年里，我欠你一份极为宝贵的建议。
senses.why: Praise for help uses the same logic: advice can cost nothing yet be priceless.
senses.whyCN: 对帮助的赞美沿用同一逻辑：建议可能分文不花，却价值连城。

senses.title: Precious but fragile
senses.definition: emphasizing that something precious is easily lost and must be protected
senses.definitionCN: 强调珍贵之物容易失去、需要保护
senses.example: The collection is invaluable and must be kept in a safe room.
senses.exampleCN: 这批藏品极为珍贵，必须存放在安全的房间里。
senses.why: Things that cannot be priced cannot be insured easily either, so the word often carries a warning.
senses.whyCN: 无法标价的东西也不太容易投保，因此这个词常常带出「需要小心保护」的警告。

intro.en: Invaluable is in- plus valuable, a word built on the Latin verb valere, to be worth.
intro.cn: invaluable 由前缀 in- 加 valuable 构成，valuable 的根是拉丁语动词 valere（值、有价值）。

items.en: Valere means to be strong, to be worth, or to have value.
items.cn: valere 意为强壮、值钱、有价值。

items.en: Value comes into French from Latin, meaning worth.
items.cn: value 从拉丁语进入法语，意为价值。

items.en: Valuable appears in English, meaning having worth, from value plus -able.
items.cn: valuable 进入英语，意为「有价值的」，由 value 加词尾 -able 构成。

items.en: Invaluable arises as in- before v-, where the negative in- forbids valuing rather than stating worth.
items.cn: invaluable 出现，「不」加在 valuation 上，否定的是「估价」这一动作。

items.en: The word settles into its paradoxical sense: too precious to be valued.
items.cn: 词义稳定为乍看矛盾的「无价到无法估价」。

note.en: Invaluable looks like it should mean without value, but in- here negates valuing, and its true neighbours are priceless and precious.
note.cn: invaluable 看起来像「没有价值」，但 in- 否定的是「估价」，它与 priceless、precious 才是近邻。

entries.definition: worth a lot of money or of great importance
entries.definitionCN: 贵重的；有价值的（去掉 in- 的肯定形式）

entries.definition: having no worth at all
entries.definitionCN: 一文不值的；与 invaluable 意思正好相反

entries.definition: to assess the worth or quality of something
so precious that no price can be named
of great value because it is rare or loved
entries.definitionCN: 宝贵的；珍贵的（侧重稀有与被珍爱）

entries.definition: so necessary that it cannot be done without
entries.definitionCN: 必不可少的；不可或缺的

normalIntro.en: Invaluable traps every learner: in- usually means not, yet here it negates valuing, which leaves us with worth beyond all price.
normalIntro.cn: invaluable 是学习者最容易跳进的坑：in- 通常表示「不」，但这里否定的是估价，剩下的是无法用价格衡量的价值。

normal.en: Valuable is what has a price; invaluable is what breaks the price tag.
normal.cn: valuable 是有价格的东西，invaluable 是撑破价签的东西。

normal.en: Read in- as cannot be valued, not as worthless.
normal.cn: 把 in- 读作「无法估价」，而不是「价值为零」。

normal.en: Valueless means no worth; invaluable means too much worth.
normal.cn: valueless 表示毫无价值，invaluable 表示价值高得装不下。

normal.en: The verb evaluate shares the root: you evaluate what has worth.
normal.cn: 动词 evaluate 同根：你去评估的，都是有价值的东西。

normal.en: In IELTS essays, invaluable help or advice sounds far warmer than very useful help.
normal.cn: 在雅思写作里，invaluable help 或 invaluable advice 比 very useful help 温暖得多。

abstract.en: See a scale with no numbers: the needle has slipped off the end.
abstract.cn: 想象一杆没有刻度的秤，指针已经滑到了尽头之外。

abstract.en: Picture a price tag turned over and written on the back: cannot be sold.
abstract.cn: 想象一张价签被翻到背面，上面写着「非卖品」。

abstract.en: Imagine a single photo album carrying an entire family history.
abstract.cn: 想象一本相册装着整个家族的历史。

examples.en: The old letters proved invaluable to the historian.
examples.cn: 这些旧信件对历史学家来说极有价值。

examples.en: Her advice on the interview was invaluable.
examples.cn: 她对面试的建议极为宝贵。

examples.en: Volunteers were invaluable in the search for the missing child.
examples.cn: 在寻找失踪儿童的过程中，志愿者发挥了不可替代的作用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因保姆」——请来一位好保姆，家里处处受益，堪称无价之宝；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 valere（强壮、值、有价值）→ value（价值）→ valuable（有价值的）→ 加否定前缀 in- 构成 invaluable，字面义「无法估价的」，核心义「珍贵到无法标价」。

sensesIntro.en: Invaluable begins with the literal refusal to price something, then extends to extreme usefulness, an irreplaceable resource, praise for rare help, and finally a warning that what is priceless is fragile.
sensesIntro.cn: invaluable 先由「拒绝给某物标价」的字面义出发，扩展到「极其有用」「不可替代的资源」「对难得帮助的赞美」，最后带出「珍贵而脆弱」的警示。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a treasure whose price tag has no number on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件宝物，价签上任何数字都写不下。

branches.en: Beyond-price worth is the literal heart of the word.
branches.cn: 超过价格的价值是这个词的字面核心。

branches.en: Practical usefulness is the everyday IELTS sense.
branches.cn: 实际用处是雅思语境中最常见的义项。

branches.en: An irreplaceable resource grows from the same unpriced worth.
branches.cn: 不可替代的资源同样源自无法定价的价值。

branches.en: Praise for advice and help is the social use of the word.
branches.cn: 对建议与帮助的赞美是这个词语用层面的社交用法。

branches.en: Both price and treasured objects are things one loses or keeps.
branches.cn: 高价值与珍贵之物都面临「失去还是守住」的问题。

intro.en: Invaluable is built from the negative prefix in- and valuable, on the Latin root val- meaning to be worth.
intro.cn: invaluable 由否定前缀 in- 与 valuable 构成，共同基于拉丁词根 val-（值、有价值）。

latinIntro.en: Latin valere means to be strong or to be worth, and English gained value, valid, and evaluate from it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 valere 意为强壮或值钱，英语由它得到 value、valid、evaluate 等词。

items.meaning: to be worth, to be strong
items.example: Valere is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: valere 是整组词根的来源。

items.meaning: worth, or to consider as worth
items.example: Value turns the Latin verb into a noun.
items.exampleCN: value 把拉丁动词变成名词。

items.example: Valuable is the value plus the suffix -able.
items.exampleCN: valuable 由 value 加词尾 -able 构成。

items.example: Valuable is the base form of the entry.
items.exampleCN: valuable 是本词条的肯定形式。

items.example: The prefix in- negates the word it joins.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 否定它所附加的词。

items.example: Invaluable negates valuing, not worth.
items.exampleCN: invaluable 否定的是估价，而不是价值。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms invaluably.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 invaluably。

items.example: Priceless uses the same logic with the word price.
items.exampleCN: priceless 用 price 一词走同样的构词逻辑。

items.example: Valueless shows the other direction of the -less suffix.
items.exampleCN: valueless 展示词尾 -less 的另一种方向。

items.example: Evaluate keeps the act of valuing alive.
items.exampleCN: evaluate 保留了「估价」这一动作。

latinEntries.meaning: to be worth, to be strong

definition_zh: 不变性；恒定性；不变态；对变换的保持
definition_en: the quality of staying the same when conditions change, especially a property that a transformation leaves unchanged
core_image: 一个方框在旋转、缩放与翻转之后，内部的图案始终原样不动
scene: 实验室里，研究员把同一样本放进不同的温度循环，测得的读数和最初一次几乎一样。The team reported invariance in the readings across every temperature cycle.
sceneCN: 这里 invariance 是「不变性」（第 1 个义项：条件改变时数值或性质保持不变）；句意：团队报告说，无论温度循环多少次，读数都保持不变。

collocations.zh: 尺度不变性；标度不变性

derivatives.zh: 不变的；不变量，由 -ance 改回 -ant 得到
方差；差异；变化，去掉否定前缀 in- 的肯定形式
改变；变化，词根动词
可变性；变异性，与 invariance 构成反义对照

senses.title: Staying the same under change
senses.definition: the state of remaining unchanged while external conditions shift
senses.definitionCN: 外部条件改变时仍保持不变的状态
senses.example: The invariance of the results surprised the whole lab.
senses.exampleCN: 结果保持不变，这让整个实验室都很意外。
senses.why: The prefix in- reverses variance, so the word names the very absence of change and variation.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 in- 翻转 variance（变化、方差）的含义，所以这个词命名的是「变化本身的缺席」。

senses.title: A property untouched by transformation
senses.definition: a quantity or property that stays the same after a change of coordinates, scale, or frame
senses.definitionCN: 在改变坐标系、尺度或参照系之后仍保持不变的量或性质
senses.example: Physicists look for invariance under rotation.
senses.exampleCN: 物理学家寻找在旋转下保持不变的性质。
senses.why: If a quantity survives every way of looking at it, it belongs to the thing itself rather than to the observer.
senses.whyCN: 如果某个量在任何观察方式下都不变，它属于事物本身，而不属于观察者。

senses.title: Sameness across groups
senses.definition: the condition in which a measurement or rule works the same way for different groups or fields
senses.definitionCN: 某项测量或规律在不同群体、不同领域中同样成立的状态
senses.example: The study tested the invariance of the scale across languages.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究检验了该量表在不同语言间是否等价。
senses.why: When a measuring tool behaves identically for everyone, the tool itself is said to be invariant.
senses.whyCN: 当同一个测量工具对所有人表现一致时，我们说这个工具具有不变性。

senses.title: Fixed pattern of behaviour
senses.definition: an unvarying pattern of behaviour that resists new situations
senses.definitionCN: 不随情境变化、抗拒新规则的行为模式
senses.example: Rigid invariance in routine makes change hard to accept.
senses.exampleCN: 例行公事里顽固的不变性让变化难以被接受。
senses.why: The technical sense borrows an everyday meaning when people themselves refuse to adapt.
senses.whyCN: 当人拒绝适应时，技术义项被借到日常语境，指人的「不可改变」。

senses.title: A constant worth relying on
senses.definition: a stable feature that can be trusted because it does not waver
senses.definitionCN: 稳定可靠、从不摇摆的特征
senses.example: Her calm shows an invariance that colleagues lean on.
senses.exampleCN: 她的镇定呈现出一种恒常性，同事们都能依靠。
senses.why: What stays the same can be predicted, so invariance quietly becomes a word for reliability.
senses.whyCN: 保持不变的东西可以被预测，于是 invariance 悄悄变成「可靠」的代名词。

intro.en: Invariance is in- plus variance, whose Latin root variare means to vary or change.
intro.cn: invariance 由前缀 in- 加 variance 构成，variance 的拉丁词根 variare 意为「变化、改变」。

items.en: Variare means to change or make different, related to varius, meaning varied.
items.cn: variare 意为改变或使不同，与 varius（杂色的、多样的）相关。

items.en: Variance enters English through French, naming disagreement or change.
items.cn: variance 经法语进入英语，指分歧或变化。

items.en: Invariance forms by adding the negative prefix in- to variance.
items.cn: invariance 由否定前缀 in- 加 variance 形成。

items.en: Mathematics adopts invariance for properties preserved by transformations.
items.cn: 数学采用 invariance 指变换下保持不变的性质。

items.en: Statistics and social science extend invariance to measurement equivalence.
items.cn: 统计学与社会科学把 invariance 扩展到测量等价性。

note.en: Invariance sits with its own family, invariant and variance, and with the statistics word stability.
note.cn: invariance 与自己的词族 invariant、variance 相伴，也与统计学中的「稳定性」邻近。

entries.definition: unchanging, or a quantity that does not change
a difference or amount of change, or the spread in statistics
entries.definitionCN: 差异；变化幅度；统计上的方差

entries.definition: never changing or varying
entries.definitionCN: 不变的；恒定不变的（形容词形式）

entries.definition: the quality of staying the same over time
the state of being steady and unlikely to change
the state of being equal in value or meaning

normalIntro.en: Invariance takes the everyday word variance and puts a firm not in front of it, turning change into the absence of change.
normalIntro.cn: invariance 把日常词 variance 前面钉上一个「不」，于是「变化」变成了「没有变化」。

normal.en: Variance names the churn; in- variance names the calm that churn cannot disturb.
normal.cn: variance 说的是翻腾，in- 加 variance 说的是翻腾也扰不动的平静。

normal.en: Invariant is the adjective; invariance is the property it names.
normal.cn: invariant 是形容词，invariance 是它所命名的那种性质。

normal.en: In physics, invariance under rotation means the same law from any angle.
normal.cn: 在物理中，不变性 under 旋转，意味着从任何角度看规律都一样。

normal.en: In statistics, invariance across groups means one rule fits every group.
normal.cn: 在统计中，跨群体的不变性意味着同一套规则适用于所有群体。

normal.en: Vary, variable, variance, invariant, invariance share one Latin stem, variare.
normal.cn: vary、variable、variance、invariant、invariance 共享同一个拉丁词干 variare。

abstract.en: Rotate a square and the shape has the same outline every quarter turn.
abstract.cn: 让正方形每转四分之一圈转一次，轮廓始终一模一样。

abstract.en: Put a ruler into any room and it measures the same length.
abstract.cn: 把同一把尺子放进任何房间，量出的长度都一样。

abstract.en: Think of a lighthouse whose light spins but never changes.
abstract.cn: 想象一座灯塔，光在旋转，亮度始终不变。

examples.en: The experiment tested the invariance of the pattern over time.
examples.cn: 实验检验了这一模式随时间是否保持不变。

examples.en: Invariance under rotation makes the law simple to state.
examples.cn: 在旋转下保持不变，使这条定律表述起来很简单。

examples.en: Researchers checked the invariance of the test in five countries.
examples.cn: 研究者检验了该测验在五个国家间是否等价。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「印万雷安斯」——无论什么都印一万遍，结果还是原样，即「不变性」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 variare（使变化，与 varius「多样的」相关）→ variance（变化、分歧）→ 加否定前缀 in- 构成 invariance，核心义「变不了」。

sensesIntro.en: Invariance starts as the pure absence of change, hardens into a mathematical property preserved by transformations, widens to sameness across groups, and finally reaches rigid human habits and dependable constancy.
sensesIntro.cn: invariance 先指纯粹「无变化」的状态，在数学中凝成变换下保持的性质，再扩展到跨群体的一致，最后落到人的行为定式与可靠恒常。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shape that looks the same after any move.
core.cn: 核心意象：无论怎样挪动，图案看上去都一样。

branches.en: The plain sense is simply not changing.
branches.cn: 基础义就是「没有改变」。

branches.en: Mathematics narrows this to properties kept by transformations.
branches.cn: 数学把它收窄为变换下保持的性质。

branches.en: Sameness across groups is the measurement sense.
branches.cn: 跨群体的一致是测量层面的义项。

branches.en: Rigid habit is the human everyday sense.
branches.cn: 行为定式是日常语境中关于人的义项。

branches.en: Both a stable number and a reliable person refuse to waver.
branches.cn: 稳定的数值与可靠的人，都拒绝摇摆。

intro.en: Invariance joins the negative prefix in- to the noun variance, whose root vari- appears in vary, variable, and various.
intro.cn: invariance 由否定前缀 in- 与名词 variance 结合，词根 vari- 也出现在 vary、variable、various 中。

latinIntro.en: Latin variare means to change, and varius means varied; the family first meant a changing of state.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 variare 意为改变，varius 意为多样的；这组词最初表示状态的变化。

items.example: Variare gives the whole family its sense of change.
items.exampleCN: variare 为整组词提供「变化」的含义。

items.example: Vary is the plain English verb from the root.
items.exampleCN: vary 是源自该词根的朴素动词。

items.example: The suffix -ance turns an adjective into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ance 把形容词变成名词。

items.example: Variance names the changing itself.
items.exampleCN: variance 命名「变化」本身。

items.example: The prefix in- reverses variance.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 翻转 variance 的含义。

items.example: Invariance is the entry word.
items.exampleCN: invariance 是本词条的目标词。

items.example: Invariant is the adjective of the noun.
items.exampleCN: invariant 是该名词的形容词形式。

items.example: Variable builds on the same root.
items.exampleCN: variable 建立在同一词根上。

items.example: Variable marks what cannot be fixed.
items.exampleCN: variable 标记仍然会变的东西。

items.example: Various keeps the Latin sense of variety.
items.exampleCN: various 保留拉丁语中「多样」的含义。

definition_zh: 有创造力的；善于发明的；新颖独创的
definition_en: good at thinking of new ideas and original ways of doing things
core_image: 一个人推开旧图纸，在白纸上画出前人从未画过他的一台机器
scene: 学校的机器人比赛还剩最后一小时，小组里的女孩拆掉旧车的底盘，用橡皮筋搭出一个全新的抓取装置。The task was slow, so an inventive girl rebuilt the grabber from spare parts.
sceneCN: 这里 inventive 是「有创造力的、善于发明的」（第 1 个义项：能想到新点子）；句意：任务进展太慢，于是一位善于发明的女孩用零件重新做成了抓取装置。

pos.zh: 有创造力的；善于发明的

derivatives.zh: 创造性；独创性，由 inventive 加词尾 -ness 构成
富有创意地，由 inventive 加 -ly 构成
发明；创造，词根动词
发明；发明物，由 invent 加 -ion 构成
发明者；发明家，由 invent 加 -or 构成

senses.title: Good at coming up with new ideas
senses.titleCN: 有创造力的；善于发明的
senses.definition: naturally able to imagine and create things that did not exist before
senses.definitionCN: 天生善于想象并创造出前所未有的事物
senses.example: She is an inventive designer who hates copying.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一位讨厌抄袭、富有创造力的设计师。
senses.why: The Latin root invenire means to come upon or find, so an inventive person is one who keeps finding new things.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 invenire 意为「遇到、找到」，所以善于发明的人就是总能把新东西「找」出来的人。

senses.title: Original and clever in method
senses.definition: original and clever, especially in the way something is done or made
senses.definitionCN: 在做法或制作方式上新颖而巧妙
senses.example: Their approach to waste sorting was strikingly inventive.
senses.exampleCN: 他们处理垃圾分类的方法独特而巧妙。
senses.why: The finding quality moves from the person to the method: what is inventive has never been done that way before.
senses.whyCN: 这种「找到新办法」的特质从人转移到方法上：凡是 inventive 的事，都没人这样做过。

senses.title: Rich in original ideas
senses.titleCN: 充满创意的；别出心裁的
senses.definition: full of fresh ideas, as a piece of work or a period may be
senses.definitionCN: 作品或某个时期充满新颖想法
senses.example: The film is inventive in every frame.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影每一帧都别出心裁。
senses.why: When ideas flow freely, the whole product, not only its maker, earns the label.
senses.whyCN: 当创意源源不断时，得到这个评价的不只是创作者，而是整件作品。

senses.title: Resourceful under constraint
senses.titleCN: 急中生智的；善用资源的
senses.definition: quick at finding clever solutions when resources are scarce
senses.definitionCN: 资源不足时能迅速想出巧妙解决办法
senses.example: The villagers were inventive when the bridge was washed away.
senses.exampleCN: 桥被冲走后，村民们急中生智。
senses.why: Finding implies searching with limited means, so pressure can make inventiveness visible.
senses.whyCN: 「寻找」意味着在有限条件下摸索，所以压力往往让创造力显现出来。

senses.title: Fabricated rather than true
senses.definition: used, usually critically, of details or excuses that are made up rather than real
senses.definitionCN: 多含批评意味，指细节或借口是凭空编造而非真实的
senses.example: His inventive excuse fooled no one in the office.
senses.exampleCN: 他那个编造出来的借口在办公室里谁也没骗过。
senses.why: Inventing can also mean making something up, so inventive may turn from praise into mild criticism of a made-up story.
senses.whyCN: invent 也可指「编造」，于是 inventive 会从褒义转向对「编出来的东西」的轻微批评。

intro.en: Inventive comes from Latin invenire, to come upon or find, through the English verb invent and the suffix -ive.
intro.cn: inventive 源自拉丁语 invenire（遇到、找到），经英语动词 invent 加词尾 -ive 构成。

items.en: Invenire combines in- meaning into with venire meaning to come, so it means to come upon.
items.cn: invenire 由 in-（进入）与 venire（来）组成，意为「遇见、找到」。

items.en: Inventio names the act of finding or discovering something.
items.cn: inventio 指发现或找到某物的行为。

items.en: Invent appears in English, first meaning to discover or devise.
items.cn: invent 进入英语，最初意为发现或设想。

items.en: Inventive forms from invent and the suffix -ive, meaning having the power to invent.
items.cn: inventive 由 invent 加词尾 -ive 构成，意为「具有发明能力的」。

items.en: Modern English widens the word from inventors to any clever, original mind or work.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词从发明家扩展到任何富有创意的人和作品。

note.en: Inventive shares its Latin root with invent, invention, and inventor, and stands close to creative and imaginative.
note.cn: inventive 与 invent、invention、inventor 同根，与 creative、imaginative 意义相近。

entries.definition: to create something that did not exist before
a thing or process that has been invented
a person who invents things
able to produce new and original ideas or work
entries.definitionCN: 有创造力的（更泛指艺术与想法）

entries.definition: good at imagining unusual things or ideas
clever, original, and effective at solving problems
entries.definitionCN: 巧妙的；聪慧有创意的（侧动脑筋与巧思）

normalIntro.en: Inventive is invent plus -ive: the doing follows the finding, and the inventor is the one who keeps finding.
normalIntro.cn: inventive 就是 invent 加 -ive：「造」之前先「找」，发明家就是不断找到新东西的人。

normal.en: In- plus venire, to come in, gives a person who lets new ideas walk in.
normal.cn: in- 加 venire（走进来），指一个肯让新点子走进来的人。

normal.en: Invent is the verb, invention the thing, inventor the person, inventive the quality.
normal.cn: invent 是动词，invention 是东西，inventor 是人，inventive 是品质。

normal.en: Inventive describes people and methods; invented describes made-up excuses.
normal.cn: inventive 描述人和方法；invented 则常形容编造出来的借口。

normal.en: Inventive collocates with words like mind, solution, and approach.
normal.cn: inventive 常与 mind、solution、approach 等词搭配。

normal.en: In IELTS writing, inventive is a precise upgrade from very clever.
normal.cn: 在雅思写作里，inventive 是 very clever 的精准升级。

abstract.en: Picture a bare desk with nothing but a pencil and one sheet of paper.
abstract.cn: 想象一张空桌面，只有一支铅笔和一张纸。

abstract.en: Imagine a kite made from an old umbrella and a broken stick.
abstract.cn: 想象一只用旧伞和断树枝做成的风筝。

abstract.en: Think of a class where every student answers differently.
abstract.cn: 想象一个每位学生答案都不同的课堂。

examples.en: The team needed an inventive answer to a very old problem.
examples.cn: 这个团队需要一个富有创意的办法来解决一个老问题。

examples.en: She is one of the most inventive engineers in the firm.
examples.cn: 她是公司里最有创造力的工程师之一。

examples.en: His inventive use of paper made the model much cheaper.
examples.cn: 他对纸的巧妙运用让模型便宜了许多。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「殷文特」，一位叫殷文的先生特别爱琢磨新玩意，凡事都要「发明」一下；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（进入）+ venire（来）→ invenire（遇到、找到）→ inventio（发现）→ 英语 invent（发明）→ 加词尾 -ive 构成 inventive，核心义「总能找到新东西」。

sensesIntro.en: Inventive begins as a quality of people who keep finding new things, extends to original methods and idea-rich works, covers cleverness under pressure, and finally turns mildly critical when what is invented is merely made up.
sensesIntro.cn: inventive 先指人「总能找到新东西」的品质，延伸到独创的方法与充满创意的作品，再包括压力下的巧思，最后在「编造出来」的语境里带上轻微的批评色彩。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pulling a brand new object out of an empty drawer.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手从空抽屉里拉出一件全新的东西。

branches.en: A person who keeps finding is the root sense.
branches.cn: 不断找到新东西的人，是词根的原始义项。

branches.en: The original method is the applied sense in engineering and design.
branches.cn: 独创的方法，是工程与设计领域的应用义项。

branches.en: Idea-rich work is the aesthetic sense.
branches.cn: 充满创意的作品，是审美层面的义项。

branches.en: Both a clever method and a quick fix show invention under pressure.
branches.cn: 巧妙的方法与临时妙计，都展现了压力下的创造。

branches.en: The critical sense shows how inventing can turn into making up.
branches.cn: 批评义项说明「发明」也可能滑向「编造」。

intro.en: Inventive is invent plus the suffix -ive, on a Latin base in- and venire meaning to come in.
intro.cn: inventive 是 invent 加词尾 -ive，其拉丁词根由 in- 与 venire（来）构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin venire means to come, and with in- it gives invenire, to come upon; the ven- root also sits in convene and prevent.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 venire 意为来，加上 in- 得到 invenire（遇到）；ven- 词根也见于 convene、prevent。

items.example: The prefix in- means into in this word.
items.exampleCN: 在这个词里，前缀 in- 表示进入。

items.example: Venire is the coming root of the family.
items.exampleCN: venire 是这组词表示「来」的词根。

items.example: Invenire is the direct source of invent.
items.exampleCN: invenire 是 invent 的直接来源。

items.example: Invent keeps the finding sense.
items.exampleCN: invent 保留了「找到」的含义。

items.example: The suffix -ive turns invent into inventive.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ive 把 invent 变成 inventive。

items.example: Inventive is the entry word.
items.exampleCN: inventive 是本词条的目标词。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms inventiveness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 inventiveness。

items.example: Inventiveness names the quality as a noun.
items.exampleCN: inventiveness 把这种品质名词化。

items.example: The suffix -ion forms invention.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 构成 invention。

items.example: The suffix -or forms inventor.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -or 构成 inventor。

items.example: Convene shares the ven- root.
items.exampleCN: convene 共享 ven- 词根。

items.example: Prevent comes from coming before.
items.exampleCN: prevent 字面义是「先来」。

latinEntries.meaning: a finding, an act of inventing

definition_zh: 发明者；发明家；首创者
definition_en: a person who designs and creates a new device, process, or idea that did not exist before
core_image: 桌上摊满草图与零件，一个人把散落的装置拼成能用的新东西
scene: 车间的灯还亮着，地上堆满拆一半的齿轮和图纸。The young inventor tested the new engine late into the night.
sceneCN: 这里 inventor 是「发明者」（第 1 个义项：设计并造出新装置的人）；句意为这位年轻的发明者在深夜还一直在测试新发动机。

collocations.phrase: the inventor of a new method

collocations.zh: 为发明者的设计申请专利

derivatives.zh: 动词基础形，义为「发明；创造」
动词加 -ion 构成名词，义为「发明；发明物」
加 -ive 构成形容词，义为「有发明才能的」
inventive 再加 -ness，义为「创造力」

senses.title: A person who creates a new device
senses.definition: a person who designs and builds a new tool, machine, or process for the first time
senses.definitionCN: 第一次设计并造出新的工具、机器或工艺的人
senses.example: The inventor showed the crowd a small wireless lamp.
senses.exampleCN: 那位发明者向众人展示了一盏小小的无线灯。
senses.why: The Latin source means to come upon a find, so the person is one who reaches a new thing first.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为「碰上、发现」，所以这个人是第一个抵达新事物的人。

senses.title: The first author of an idea
senses.titleCN: 首创者；想出新主意的人
senses.definition: the first person to think of or devise a particular idea, method, or way of doing something
senses.definitionCN: 第一个想到某种主意、方法或做法的人
senses.example: The inventor of this teaching method is unknown.
senses.exampleCN: 这种教学法的首创者已经无从查考。
senses.why: Even when the creation is a plan rather than a machine, the man who devises it keeps the same name.
senses.whyCN: 即使创造物是方案而非机器，设计出方案的人仍用同一个词来称呼。

senses.title: A maker of false stories
senses.definition: a person who makes up a story or an excuse that is not true
senses.definitionCN: 编造不实的故事或借口的人
senses.example: The inventor of this rumour was never caught.
senses.exampleCN: 编造这个传闻的人始终没被找到。
senses.why: The verb invent can also mean to fabricate, so a maker of false tales takes the same title.
senses.whyCN: 动词 invent 也可指捏造，因此编造假故事的人也可以同样被称为发明者。

intro.en: Inventor comes from Latin inventor, a finder, from invenire, to come upon.
intro.cn: inventor 来自拉丁语 inventor（发现者），源于 invenire（遇上、找到）。

items.en: Invenire means to come upon or find, from in- plus venire, to come.
items.cn: invenire 意为遇上或找到，由 in- 加 venire（来）构成。

items.en: Inventor names the person who finds or devises something.
items.cn: inventor 指找到或想出某物的人。

items.en: Inventor passes into French as a word for a discoverer or deviser.
items.cn: inventor 进入法语，指发现者或设计者。

items.en: The word appears in English with the sense of a finder.
items.cn: 该词进入英语时仍带「发现者」的含义。

items.en: Wider use of invent for devising machines gives inventor its modern sense.
items.cn: invent 用于设计机器后广行，inventor 由此获得现代义。

items.en: Modern English also titles the author of a new idea or a false tale an inventor.
items.cn: 现代英语中，新主意的首创者或假故事的编造者也被称作 inventor。

note.en: Inventor belongs to the invent family and sits close to words for discoverers, designers, and makers.
note.cn: inventor 属于 invent 词族，与「发现者」「设计者」「制作者」一类词相邻。

entries.definition: to create something new
a new thing or the act of creating it
a full list or stock of goods
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近，意为清册、存货清单，与发明无关。

entries.definition: a person who brings something into being
a person who plans how something will look or work
a person who finds something already existing

normalIntro.en: Inventor is invented plus -or, the person ending: one who invents.
normalIntro.cn: inventor 是 invented 一族加上表示人的词尾 -or：做发明的那个人。

normal.en: Inventor shares its stem with invent, invention, and inventive.
normal.cn: inventor 与 invent、invention、inventive 同词干。

normal.en: The ending -or, as in actor and visitor, marks a person.
normal.cn: 词尾 -or 如 actor、visitor 一样标出「人」。

normal.en: The Latin verb behind it means to come upon, so the inventor arrives first at a new thing.
normal.cn: 其背后的拉丁语动词意为「碰上」，所以发明者是第一个抵达新事物的人。

normal.en: Common collocation: the inventor of the telephone.
normal.cn: 常见搭配：the inventor of the telephone，电话的发明者。

normal.en: Like other words from the verb, it can also mean a maker of stories when the verb means to fabricate.
normal.cn: 与同一动词的其他词一样，当动词指捏造时，它也可指故事的编造者。

abstract.en: Picture a hand closing around a small device that no one has held before.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手攥住一件此前没人碰过的小装置。

abstract.en: See a finger drawing the first line of a new plan on a blank sheet.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指在空白纸上画出新方案的第一笔。

abstract.en: Hear an empty room where a voice makes up a long improbable tale.
abstract.cn: 想象空房间里有个声音在编一段离谱的长故事。

examples.en: The inventor of the safety brake was a Scottish engineer.
examples.cn: 这种安全闸的发明者是一位苏格兰工程师。

examples.en: Many inventors failed dozens of times before their designs worked.
examples.cn: 许多发明者在设计成功之前失败了几十次。

examples.en: Nobody knew who was the inventor of the strange old rumour.
examples.cn: 没人知道那个离奇的旧传闻是谁编造的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因文特」——因「文」与图纸开动脑筋，特制出一样东西来；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（进入）+ venire（来）→ invenire（进来、碰上、找到）→ inventor（发现者）→ 古法语 → 英语 inventor。核心义「先一步碰上」。

sensesIntro.en: Inventor starts from the person who finds a new thing and builds the first device, then extends to the one who first thinks of an idea or makes up a story.
sensesIntro.cn: inventor 先指第一个碰上并造出新装置的人，再扩展到第一个想出主意的人，以及编造故事的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a workbench covered with sketches and parts that become a new device.
core.cn: 核心意象：堆满草图与零件的工作台，最终拼成一件新装置。

branches.en: The person who builds a new machine is the central sense.
branches.cn: 造出新机器的人是核心义项。

branches.en: The first to think of a method is the same kind of person, only without an object.
branches.cn: 第一个想出方法的人是同一类人，只是没有实体物件。

branches.en: Making up a false tale uses the verb sense to fabricate.
branches.cn: 编造假故事用的是动词「捏造」的义项。

branches.en: Both a machine and a method need someone who arrives at them first.
branches.cn: 无论机器还是方法，都需要有人先一步想到它们。

branches.en: A device that exists and a story that does not both have an author.
branches.cn: 真实存在的装置和并不存在的故事，都各有一个始作俑者。

intro.en: Inventor is the person form of invent, built from Latin in- plus venire with the agent ending -or.
intro.cn: inventor 是 invent 的人物形式，由拉丁语 in- 加 venire 并配施事后缀 -or 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin venire means to come, and invenire means to come upon or find.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 venire 意为「来」，invenire 意为「遇上、找到」。

items.example: The prefix in- brings the sense of coming into something.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 带出「进入某物」的意思。

items.example: Venire is the coming root of invenire.
items.exampleCN: venire 是 invenire 中表示「来」的词根。

items.example: Invenire joins the prefix and the coming root.
items.exampleCN: invenire 把前缀与「来」的词根合在一起。

items.example: Inventor is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: inventor 是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: Invent is the short English verb.
items.exampleCN: invent 是简短的英语动词。

items.example: The suffix -or forms actor and inventor alike.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -or 同样构成 actor 与 inventor。

items.example: The suffix -ion forms invention.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 构成 invention。

items.example: The suffix -ive forms inventive.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ive 构成 inventive。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms inventiveness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 inventiveness。

items.example: Inventive describes the skill of an inventor.
items.exampleCN: inventive 描述发明者的才能。

definition_zh: 倒置；颠倒；倒装；反转
definition_en: the act of turning something upside down or changing its usual order so that it becomes the opposite
core_image: 杯子倒扣过来，里面的东西顺着重力落回另一个容器
scene: 壶里的茶放得稍久，滤网堵住了，茶水倒得太急。A quick inversion of the cup spilled the tea onto the tray.
sceneCN: 这里 inversion 是「倒置、翻转动作」（第 1 个义项：把某物上下翻转）；句意为杯子猛地一翻，茶水洒到了托盘上。

pos.zh: 倒置；颠倒；倒装；反转；倒转

collocations.phrase: the inversion of the natural order

derivatives.zh: 动词基础形，义为「使颠倒；倒转」
过去分词转形容词，义为「倒置的；颠倒的」
加 -ible 构成形容词，义为「可逆的」
加 -ive 构成形容词，义为「倾向于颠倒的」

senses.title: The act of turning upside down
senses.definition: the act of turning something upside down or the state of being turned over
senses.definitionCN: 把某物上下翻转的动作，或倒过来的状态
senses.example: A slow inversion of the jar let the honey run out.
senses.exampleCN: 把罐子慢慢翻过来，蜂蜜就流了出来。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to turn in, and turning a thing over is the plainest bodily picture.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词意为「向内翻转」，把东西翻过来是最直观的身体动作。

senses.title: A reversal of normal order
senses.definition: a change in which the usual order of two things is swapped
senses.definitionCN: 两件事物的通常次序被互换
senses.example: The film tells its story by an inversion of time.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片用时间倒流的方式讲故事。
senses.why: If turning a thing over turns top into bottom, it also turns before into after and first into last.
senses.whyCN: 把东西翻过来，上下就互换了；同样，先后与首尾也会互换。

senses.title: Grammar: the verb before the subject
senses.definition: a sentence pattern in which the verb or auxiliary comes before the subject
senses.definitionCN: 动词或助动词出现在主语之前的句式
senses.example: Never have I seen such a storm.
senses.exampleCN: 我从没见过这样的暴风雨。
senses.why: Word order is reversed in the sentence, so grammar borrows the name of the turning-over act.
senses.whyCN: 句子里的词序被颠倒了，语法便借用了「翻转」这个名字。

senses.title: Weather: a warmer layer above a cooler one
senses.definition: a layer of warmer air lying above a layer of cooler air, trapping smog near the ground
senses.definitionCN: 较暖的空气层压在较冷的空气层之上，使雾霾滞留在近地面
senses.example: The inversion kept the smog over the city for days.
senses.exampleCN: 逆温让雾霾在城市上空盘桓了好几天。
senses.why: Normally air grows cooler with height; this pattern turns that rule upside down.
senses.whyCN: 通常空气越往上越冷，这种结构把这规律倒了个个儿。

senses.title: Physics: a change of state or direction
senses.definition: a change by which a state, a direction, or a set of levels becomes the opposite of what it was
senses.definitionCN: 某种状态、方向或能级分布变成相反的情况
senses.example: Lasers depend on a population inversion in the material.
senses.exampleCN: 激光依赖材料内的粒子数反转。
senses.why: More particles crowd a high level than a low one, so the usual pattern is turned over.
senses.whyCN: 处于高能级的粒子多于低能级，通常的分布被翻了过来。

senses.title: Music and rhetoric: an upside-down theme
