senses.definition: a melody or a borrowed phrase played or used with each of its intervals reversed
senses.definitionCN: 旋律或借用的语句把每个音程上下翻过来
senses.example: The fugue answers in inversion, climbing where the theme fell.
senses.exampleCN: 这首赋格以倒影作答，主题下行的地方它上行。
senses.why: A shape turned over keeps its outline but flips its rises into falls.
senses.whyCN: 图形翻过来后轮廓还在，只是上升变成了下降。

intro.en: Inversion comes from Latin inversio, from in- and vertere, to turn, with the noun ending -ion.
intro.cn: inversion 来自拉丁语 inversio，由 in- 与 vertere（转）加名词词尾 -ion 构成。

items.en: Vertere means to turn or bend.
items.cn: vertere 意为转、弯折。

items.en: Invertere means to turn over or reverse.
items.cn: invertere 意为翻转、倒转。

items.en: Inversio names a turning over or a reversal.
items.cn: inversio 指翻转或倒转。

items.en: Inversion enters English in the sense of turning something over.
items.cn: inversion 以「翻转」义进入英语。

items.en: Grammar, weather study, physics, and music each take the word for their own reversal.
items.cn: 语法、气象、物理与音乐各自取其「反转」义。

note.en: Inversion shares the Latin turn with invert, revert, and convert, and borders on reversal and transposition.
note.cn: inversion 与 invert、revert、convert 共享「转」的词根，并与 reversal、transposition 相邻。

entries.definition: to turn something upside down
to change into another form
to return to an earlier state
a change to the opposite direction or order
the act of swapping the position of two things
turned so that the top faces the ground

normalIntro.en: Inversion is the turning action of invert plus -ion: a turning over written as a noun.
normalIntro.cn: inversion 是 invert 的翻转动作加上 -ion：写成名词的「翻过来」。

normal.en: Inversion shares the root vertere, to turn, with invert, revert, and convert.
normal.cn: inversion 与 invert、revert、convert 共享词根 vertere，意为转。

normal.en: The prefix in- adds the sense of turning in or over.
normal.cn: 前缀 in- 带出「向内、翻转」的意思。

normal.en: The suffix -ion makes an action noun, as in action and rotation.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ion 构成动作名词，如 action、rotation。

normal.en: In grammar, inversion explains why the verb can come before the subject.
normal.cn: 语法中，inversion 解释了动词为何会排在主语之前。

normal.en: In science it names a state turned opposite, as in temperature inversion.
normal.cn: 科学中它指被翻到相反的状态，如 temperature inversion。

abstract.en: Picture a cup flipped mouth down and water held back by the air.
abstract.cn: 想象杯子杯口朝下，水被空气托住不落。

abstract.en: Imagine a queue where the last walker suddenly leads.
abstract.cn: 想象排队时排在最后的人突然走到最前。

abstract.en: Hear a tune played again with every rise turned into a fall.
abstract.cn: 想象同一支曲子再奏一遍，每个上行都变成下行。

examples.en: The inversion of the bottle let the last drops fall out.
examples.cn: 瓶子一倒过来，最后几滴就流了出来。

examples.en: English uses inversion after adverbs such as never and rarely.
examples.cn: 英语在 never、rarely 这类副词之后使用倒装。

examples.en: A temperature inversion traps cold air under a warm layer.
examples.cn: 逆温会把冷空气困在暖空气层之下。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因卧身」——在「因」为倒转而「卧」下来「身」子，整个人翻了个个儿；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（向内）+ vertere（转）→ invertere（翻转）→ inversio（翻转；倒转）→ 法语 → 英语 inversion。核心义「转过来、翻个个儿」。

sensesIntro.en: Inversion begins with a physical turning over, moves to a reversal of order, and then spreads to grammar, weather, physics, and music.
sensesIntro.cn: inversion 从物理上的翻转出发，转向次序的颠倒，再扩展到语法、气象、物理和音乐。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cup turned mouth down so that what was inside falls out.
core.cn: 核心意象：杯子杯口朝下，里面的东西落出来。

branches.en: The physical flip of an object is the base sense.
branches.cn: 物体的物理翻转是基础义项。

branches.en: Swapping the order of things is the abstract flip.
branches.cn: 互换事物次序是抽象的翻转。

branches.en: Grammar reverses the sentence order, so it takes the same name.
branches.cn: 语法里句子词序被颠倒，因此沿用同一个名字。

branches.en: Weather and physics describe states held in the opposite arrangement.
branches.cn: 气象与物理描述处于相反排列的状态。

branches.en: Music and rhetoric mirror a shape by flipping it.
branches.cn: 音乐与修辞通过翻转来镜像一个形状。

intro.en: Inversion is built from the Latin prefix in-, the root vertere, and the noun ending -ion.
intro.cn: inversion 由拉丁语前缀 in-、词根 vertere 与名词词尾 -ion 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin vertere means to turn, and invertere means to turn over.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vertere 意为转，invertere 意为翻转。

items.example: The prefix in- turns vertere into a turning inward.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 把 vertere 变成「向内翻转」。

items.example: Vertere is the turning root of the family.
items.exampleCN: vertere 是这个词族中表示「转」的词根。

items.example: Invertere joins the prefix and the root.
items.exampleCN: invertere 由前缀与词根相加而成。

items.example: Inversio is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: inversio 是直接来源。

items.example: The suffix -ion forms action nouns like inversion.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 构成 inversion 这类动作名词。

items.example: Invert is the verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: invert 是这一词族的动词。

items.example: Inverted describes something set upside down.
items.exampleCN: inverted 描述被倒置的东西。

items.example: The suffix -ible forms invertible.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ible 构成 invertible。

items.example: The prefix re- forms revert with the same root.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 与同一词根构成 revert。

items.example: The prefix con- forms convert with the same root.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 con- 与同一词根构成 convert。

items.meaning: able to be turned or reversed
items.example: Invertible is used of matrices and functions.
items.exampleCN: invertible 常用于矩阵和函数。

definition_zh: 使颠倒；倒置；倒转；反转
definition_en: to turn something upside down or to put it in the opposite position or order
core_image: 一只鞋被翻过来，鞋底朝上、鞋口朝下
scene: 下雨天，那个人走得太急，鞋里灌满了水。He stopped by the door and inverted his shoes to pour the water out.
sceneCN: 这里 invert 是「使颠倒、翻过来」（第 1 个义项：把某物上下翻转）；句意为他在门口停下，把鞋翻过来倒水。

pos.zh: 使颠倒；倒置；倒转；反转；使倒装

derivatives.zh: 动词加 -ion 构成名词，义为「倒置；倒装」
过去分词转形容词，义为「倒置的」
加表示施事的 -er，义为「逆变器；转换器」
加 -ible 构成形容词，义为「可逆的」

senses.title: To turn something upside down
senses.definition: to turn a container or object so that its top faces down
senses.definitionCN: 把容器或物件翻过来使上端朝下
senses.example: Invert the mould gently so that the cake slides out.
senses.exampleCN: 轻轻把模具倒扣，蛋糕就滑出来了。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to turn in, and flipping an object is the most direct picture of that turn.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词意为「向内转」，把物件翻过来是这一翻转最直观的画面。

senses.title: To reverse the order of things
senses.definition: to swap the positions of two things or reverse a sequence
senses.definitionCN: 互换两个事物的位置或把顺序倒过来
senses.example: The editor inverted the two paragraphs.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑把这两段调换了位置。
senses.why: Turning a thing over swaps its top and bottom, so a sequence can be turned over in the same way.
senses.whyCN: 翻过来就互换了上下，所以一个序列也可以用同样的方式翻转。

senses.title: To change a relation round
senses.titleCN: 反转；使对调（角色或关系）
senses.definition: to exchange the roles of two parties so that each takes the place of the other
senses.definitionCN: 把两方的角色对调，使各自占据对方的位置
senses.example: The new rules invert the usual relation between teacher and student.
senses.exampleCN: 新规则把师生惯常的关系反转了过来。
senses.why: Order also lives in roles, so flipping a relation means the lower becomes the higher.
senses.whyCN: 次序也存在于角色之中，把关系翻过来就是下位变上位。

senses.title: To place the verb before the subject
senses.definition: to put the verb or auxiliary in front of the subject in a sentence
senses.definitionCN: 在句中把动词或助动词放到主语之前
senses.example: The writer inverts the subject and the verb to stress the time.
senses.exampleCN: 作者把主语和动词倒装，以强调时间。
senses.why: Word order is simply flipped, so the ordinary order of a sentence goes upside down.
senses.whyCN: 词序被直接翻转，句子的通常次序就此倒了过来。

senses.title: To make an image or signal reversed
senses.definition: to make the light and dark or the polarity of an image or a signal the opposite of what it was
senses.definitionCN: 把图像或信号的明暗、极性变成相反的状态
senses.example: Click the tool that inverts the colours of the photo.
senses.exampleCN: 点击那个把照片颜色反转的工具。
senses.why: Dark and light, like top and bottom, are a pair that can be turned over.
senses.whyCN: 明与暗和上与下一样，是一对可以被翻过来的东西。

senses.title: To arrange a theme mirrored in music
senses.definition: to repeat a melody with all of its rising and falling movements reversed
senses.definitionCN: 把旋律的上升与下降全部反过来再奏一遍
senses.example: The composer inverts the theme for the second voice.
senses.exampleCN: 作曲家在第二声部把主题倒影化。
senses.why: A shape kept and flipped is a mirror image, which music calls inversion of a theme.
senses.whyCN: 保留形状再翻过来就是镜像，音乐把这种手法称为旋律倒影。

intro.en: Invert comes from Latin invertere, from in- and vertere, to turn.
intro.cn: invert 来自拉丁语 invertere，由 in- 与 vertere（转）构成。

items.en: Vertere means to turn or to bend.
items.cn: vertere 意为转、弯折。

items.en: Invertere means to turn over, overturn, or reverse.
items.cn: invertere 意为翻转、翻倒、倒转。

items.en: The verb passes into Old French as a turning-over word.
items.cn: 这个动词进入古法语，仍表示翻转。

items.en: Invert is recorded in English for turning something over.
items.cn: 英语中的 invert 已用于表示翻转某物。

items.en: Later uses extend the verb to grammar, images, and music.
items.cn: 后来的用法把该动词扩展到语法、图像与音乐。

note.en: Invert belongs to the Latin turn family, with inversion, revert, and convert, and borders on reverse and flip.
note.cn: invert 属于拉丁语「转」词族，与 inversion、revert、convert 同族，并与 reverse、flip 相邻。

entries.definition: the act of turning something over
to change one thing into another
to turn something aside
to change something to the opposite
to turn something over quickly
to turn something so its top faces down

normalIntro.en: Invert is the Latin turn root with in-, so it means to turn something inward or over.
normalIntro.cn: invert 是拉丁语「转」的词根配上前缀 in-，意为把东西转向内或翻过来。

normal.en: Invert and convert share the root vertere, to turn.
normal.cn: invert 与 convert 共享词根 vertere，意为转。

normal.en: Prefix in- points the turn inward or over.
normal.cn: 前缀 in- 把「转」指向内侧或翻转。

normal.en: The noun inversion keeps the same stem and adds -ion.
normal.cn: 名词 inversion 保留同一词干并加 -ion。

normal.en: Leave out one letter and you get the unrelated verb invite.
normal.cn: 少一个字母就成了无关的动词 invite，注意别混。

normal.en: The -ed form inverted works as an adjective, as in inverted commas.
normal.cn: -ed 形式 inverted 可作形容词，如 inverted commas（引号）。

abstract.en: See a wet shoe lifted and tipped so the water runs out.
abstract.cn: 想象抬起一只湿鞋往下倒，让水流出来。

abstract.en: Picture a row of cards shuffled so the first becomes the last.
abstract.cn: 想象一排卡片被倒序摊开，第一张成了最后一张。

abstract.en: Hear two people swap seats, the quiet listener now giving the lecture.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人换了座位，原本安静听讲的人现在讲起课来。

examples.en: Invert the glass on the paper so the air cannot get in.
examples.cn: 把玻璃杯倒扣在纸上，空气就进不去了。

examples.en: The designer inverted the order of the two panels.
examples.cn: 设计师把两块面板的次序对调了。

examples.en: Writers sometimes invert the word order for emphasis.
examples.cn: 写作者有时会颠倒词序以加强语气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因我特」——正是「因」为我特意把碗翻过来扣住，才倒着放；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（向内）+ vertere（转）→ invertere（翻转、倒转）→ 古法语 → 英语 invert。核心义「转过来、翻个个儿」。

sensesIntro.en: Invert starts from physically turning an object over and widens to reversed order, exchanged roles, grammar, images, and music.
sensesIntro.cn: invert 从把物体物理翻转开始，扩展到次序颠倒、角色对调，以及语法、图像与音乐。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shoe turned over so that its sole faces up.
core.cn: 核心意象：鞋被翻过来，鞋底朝上。

branches.en: Turning a physical object over is the base sense.
branches.cn: 翻转实物是基础义项。

branches.en: Reversing a sequence is the turn applied to order.
branches.cn: 颠倒序列是把翻转用在次序上。

branches.en: Exchanging roles flips a relation between two sides.
branches.cn: 对调角色是把两方的关系翻过来。

branches.en: Grammar and imaging reverse a fixed pattern of word or light.
branches.cn: 语法与成像反转固定的词序或明暗样式。

branches.en: Music mirrors a melody by flipping its every movement.
branches.cn: 音乐通过翻转每个走向来镜像旋律。

intro.en: Invert pairs the Latin prefix in- with the root vertere, which also builds convert, divert, and revert.
intro.cn: invert 由拉丁语前缀 in- 与词根 vertere 组成，后一词根还构成 convert、divert、revert。

latinIntro.en: Latin vertere means to turn, and invertere means to turn over.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vertere 意为转，invertere 意为翻转。

items.example: The prefix in- makes the turn go inward.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 让这个「转」转向内侧。

items.example: Vertere is the shared turning root.
items.exampleCN: vertere 是共同的「转」词根。

items.example: Invertere is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: invertere 是直接的拉丁语来源。

items.example: The suffix -ion turns invert into inversion.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 把 invert 变成 inversion。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms inverted.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 inverted。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does
items.example: The suffix -er forms inverter.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 inverter。

items.example: The suffix -ible forms invertible.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ible 构成 invertible。

items.example: The prefix con- forms convert from the same root.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 con- 用同一词根构成 convert。

items.example: The prefix di- forms divert from the same root.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 di- 用同一词根构成 divert。

items.example: The prefix re- forms revert from the same root.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 用同一词根构成 revert。

items.meaning: a device that changes direct current to alternating current
items.example: An inverter changes direct current into alternating current.
items.exampleCN: 逆变器把直流电变成交流电。

definition_zh: 不可侵犯的；不可违背的；神圣不可亵渎的；不可亵渎的
definition_en: so strong or sacred that it must not be broken, entered, or treated with disrespect
core_image: 石碑上刻着一条界线，旁边插着一块写有禁止越线的木牌，没有人敢跨过去
scene: 战后写成的宪法在首条就写明，个人的尊严与隐私不容任何人染指。The court ruled that basic human dignity is inviolable, whatever the emergency.
sceneCN: 这里 inviolable 是「不可侵犯的」（第 1 个义项：权利或边界不容他人触碰）；句意为法院裁定，无论遇到何种紧急状况，人的基本尊严都不可侵犯。

pos.zh: 不可侵犯的；不可违背的；神圣的

collocations.zh: 把某事物视为神圣不可侵犯

derivatives.zh: 基础动词，义为「违反；侵犯；亵渎」
由 violate 加 -ion 构成，义为「违反；侵犯；亵渎」
由词根加 -able 构成，义为「可被破坏的；可被侵犯的」，与本词构成反义对照
由本词加 -ity 构成，义为「不可侵犯性；不可违背性」
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「不可侵犯地」

senses.title: Too sacred or precious to be touched
senses.titleCN: 不可侵犯的；不容触碰的
senses.definition: treated as too sacred or precious to be attacked, entered, or interfered with
senses.definitionCN: 被看得过于神圣或宝贵，不许攻击、闯入或干涉
senses.example: The treaty declares the temple grounds inviolable.
senses.exampleCN: 条约宣布寺庙的院地不可侵犯。
senses.why: The prefix in- reverses violable, and Latin violare meant to treat with force; what cannot be violated is fenced off by reverence.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 in- 把 violable 反过来，拉丁语 violare 意为「以强力对待」；不能 violare 的东西因为受到敬重而被围上栅栏。

senses.title: A right or rule that cannot be broken
senses.definition: describing a right, rule, or promise so basic that breaking it is not allowed
senses.definitionCN: 形容权利、规则或承诺极为基本，不允许被破坏
senses.example: Freedom of thought is an inviolable right in a free society.
senses.exampleCN: 在自由社会里，思想自由是一项不可侵犯的权利。
senses.why: The same fence now marks a moral or legal boundary: to cross it is an offence, so the rule stays whole and unbroken.
senses.whyCN: 同一道栅栏现在划在道德或法律的界线上：越过它就是过错，所以这条规则始终完整、未被破坏。

senses.title: A border or secret kept from entry
senses.titleCN: 不可侵入的；不可泄露的
senses.definition: describing a place, border, or piece of information that no outsider is permitted to enter or reveal
senses.definitionCN: 形容地点、边界或信息不允许外人进入或泄露
senses.example: The old archive is inviolable and open only to the keeper.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧档案馆不可擅入，只有保管人能进。
senses.why: When the fence stands on physical ground, inviolable turns into a guarded door that lets nobody through.
senses.whyCN: 当这道栅栏落在现实的地面上，inviolable 就变成一扇把所有人挡在门外的守门。

senses.title: Formal and emphatic, in argument
senses.titleCN: （正式或反讽）断然不容置疑的
senses.definition: used formally, sometimes ironically, to say that a view or ruling must not be questioned at all
senses.definitionCN: 正式使用，有时带反讽，表示某种看法或裁定断然不容质疑
senses.example: The speaker treated his own opinion as inviolable and refused all questions.
senses.exampleCN: 发言人把自己的意见当作不容置疑，拒绝一切提问。
senses.why: The word reaches beyond law into tone: a statement that is fenced off from all challenge sounds solemn, and can sound pompous.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从法律延伸到语气：被栅栏围起来、不容任何质疑的说法，听起来庄重，也可能显得自以为是。

intro.en: Inviolable is built from the Latin verb violare, to treat with force, with the prefix in- meaning not.
intro.cn: inviolable 由拉丁语动词 violare（以强力对待）加否定前缀 in-（不）构成。

items.en: The root behind violare is generally reconstructed as *wi-, denoting force or violence. Its deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: violare 背后的词根一般认为可重构为 *wi-，表示「强力、暴力」；更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Violare meant to treat with force or dishonour, and also to break a rule or desecrate a sacred thing.
items.cn: violare 意为「以强力或不敬对待」，也指破坏规则或亵渎神圣之物。

items.en: The adjective violabilis was formed early with the suffix -bilis, meaning able to be violated.
items.cn: 早期用词尾 -bilis 构成形容词 violabilis，意为「可被侵犯的」。

items.en: Adding in- negated the adjective: inviolabilis described sanctuary, oaths and persons that must not be harmed.
items.cn: 加上 in- 否定这个形容词：inviolabilis 用来形容不可加害的圣地、誓言与人身。

items.en: The word reached English through French worship sources, first in religious and legal settings; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词经由宗教与法律用语的渠道进入英语，最早见于宗教与法律场景；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Today it covers sacred places, basic rights, borders and promises, and can also be used with irony.
items.cn: 今天它覆盖圣地、基本权利、边界与承诺，也可以带反讽地使用。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same violate family; the near-meaning group gathers words for things that must not be broken or crossed.
note.cn: 形近组收 violate 这一词族的词；近义组收表示「不许破坏、不许越过」的词。

entries.definition: To break a rule, promise, or right, or to treat something sacred with contempt.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「违反、侵犯、亵渎」，是本词词族的基础动词。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of breaking a rule or intruding on a right.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「违反、侵犯」，由 violate 加 -ion 构成。

entries.definition: Able to be broken or violated; the positive form that in- negates.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可被破坏的」，是被 in- 否定的肯定形式。

entries.definition: In a forceful and harmful way; built on the same force root.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「猛烈地、暴力地」，同源于表示强力的词根。

entries.definition: Force used to harm people or damage things.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「暴力、强力」，与本词共享表示强力的词根。

entries.definition: Connected with God or religion and treated with deep respect, though not necessarily protected by law.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「神圣的」，因宗教而受敬重，不一定有法律保护。

entries.definition: Impossible to break, whether physically or as a promise.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「牢不可破的」，兼指实物与承诺。

entries.definition: Not allowed to be touched or criticised, but used in everyday speech rather than legal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「碰不得的、动不得的」，偏口语，不如本词正式。

entries.definition: Unable to be defeated; it merely looks like this word and comes from Latin vincere, to conquer.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不可战胜的」；只是拼写相近，词源不同，出自拉丁语 vincere（征服）。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin family of violare and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用 violare 的真实拉丁词族，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Violate is the action; inviolable is the state of something that has been fenced off from that action.
normal.cn: violate 是动作；inviolable 是被栅栏隔开、不会受到这个动作的状态。

normal.en: In- plus violable equals not able to be violated, just as illegal means not lawful.
normal.cn: in- 加 violable 就是「不能被侵犯的」，如同 illegal 表示不合法的。

normal.en: A human right is usually called an inviolable right, and a basic principle an inviolable principle.
normal.cn: 基本权利常说成 inviolable right，基本原则常说成 inviolable principle。

normal.en: Inviolable keeps its exact Latin shape, while violation and violence took shorter routes into English.
normal.cn: inviolable 保留了拉丁语原貌，而 violation 与 violence 走的是较短的入英语路径。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with invincible, which comes from conquering rather than from force against a boundary.
normal.cn: 别和 invincible 混淆，后者来自「征服」，不涉及对界限的强力。

abstract.en: Picture a stone tablet with a line cut across it and a sign standing beside the line.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石碑，上面刻着一条线，线旁立着一块牌子。

abstract.en: See a hand raised in front of a doorway: nobody passes through it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手举在门口：谁也不能穿过去。

abstract.en: Imagine a seal on a letter that no one is allowed to break open.
abstract.cn: 想象一封信上盖着封条，谁都不许拆开。

examples.en: Personal liberty is treated as inviolable in the constitution.
examples.cn: 宪法把人身自由视为不可侵犯。

examples.en: The ambassador reminded both states that their common border was inviolable.
examples.cn: 大使提醒两国，它们共同的边界不可侵犯。

examples.en: For the old monk, the silence of the shrine was inviolable.
examples.cn: 对那位老僧人来说，神龛的寂静不可打扰。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「银外尔伯」——银子放在外面，有伯爷守着，任何人都靠近不得：不可侵犯

root: 由拉丁语前缀 in-（不）+ 动词 violare（以强力对待）派生形容词 violabilis（可被侵犯的），再加上否定前缀，形成晚期拉丁语 inviolabilis（不可侵犯的）；英语十五世纪经法语渠道借入。同根词有 violate、violation、violence，核心意象是「围着一道不许越过的界」。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses all draw one fence around something: a sacred place first, then a right or rule, then a border or secret, and finally a tone of argument that refuses all challenge.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项都在同一个对象外面围一道界：先是圣地，再是权利或规则，然后是边界或机密，最后是拒绝一切质疑的论辩语气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boundary is cut into stone and a sign beside it forbids crossing.
core.cn: 核心意象：界址刻在石上，旁边一块牌子禁止越界。

branches.en: THE SACRED: reverence keeps the place from being entered or harmed.
branches.cn: 神圣线：敬畏把地点保护起来，不许进入，不许加害。

branches.en: THE RULE: the fence stands on a right or principle and makes breaking it an offence.
branches.cn: 规则线：栅栏立在权利或原则上，破坏它就构成过错。

branches.en: THE BORDER: on real ground the same fence becomes a guarded door or sealed file.
branches.cn: 边界线：在现实地面上，同一道栅栏变成守门的门禁或封存的档案。

branches.en: THE TONE: the word moves from law into argument, where it sounds solemn or pompous.
branches.cn: 语气线：这个词从法律走进论辩，听起来庄重，也可能显得自负。

branches.en: Both the sacred place and the basic right survive because nobody is allowed to use force on them.
branches.cn: 圣地与基本权利之所以完好，都因为不允许对它们施加强力。

intro.en: Inviolable is a Latin prefix in- plus a Latin stem and the suffix -able, with English adding -ity and -ly.
intro.cn: inviolable 是拉丁语前缀 in- 加拉丁词干与词尾 -able，英语再加上 -ity 与 -ly。

latinIntro.en: Latin violare, violabilis and inviolabilis are all recorded forms, so only the deeper force root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 violare、violabilis 与 inviolabilis 都有文献记录，只有更深层的「强力」词根属于重构形式。

items.example: The prefix turns violable into its opposite.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把 violable 变成它的反义。

items.meaning: to treat with force, break, desecrate
items.example: The verb supplies the core idea of force.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「强力」的核心含义。

items.example: The suffix -bilis makes the stem into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -bilis 把词干变成形容词。

items.example: It forms words such as violable and breakable.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 violable、breakable 这类词。

items.meaning: not to be broken or entered
items.meaningCN: 不可破坏的；不可进入的
items.example: The adjective keeps the full Latin shape.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词保留了完整的拉丁语形态。

items.example: It forms inviolability.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 inviolability。

items.example: It forms inviolably.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 inviolably。

items.example: Violate keeps the action of the Latin verb.
items.exampleCN: violate 保留了拉丁语动词的动作含义。

items.meaning: the act of breaking a rule
items.example: The suffix -ion names the act.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 表示这一行为。

definition_zh: 援引；援用；引用；祈求；唤起；调用
definition_en: to call on someone or something for help, support, or authority, or to bring something into action
core_image: 一个人举起手，朝高处大声喊出一个名字，被叫到的存在随即应声而来
scene: 律师在结案陈词里搬出多年前的一条旧判决，为自己一方撑腰。The defence lawyer invoked an old ruling from the same court to support her argument.
sceneCN: 这里 invoke 是「援引、搬出」（第 2 个义项：引用法律或条款作为依据）；句意为辩方律师援引同一法院的一条旧判决来支持自己的论据。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ation 构成，义为「祈求；援引；召唤仪式」
由 invocation 加 -y 构成，义为「祈求式的；召唤用的」
同根不同前缀，re-「回」加 vocare「呼唤」，义为「撤销；撤回」
同根不同前缀，pro-「向前」加 vocare「呼唤」，义为「激起；挑动」
同根不同前缀，e-「向外」加 vocare「呼唤」，义为「唤起；引起」

senses.title: To call on a god for help
senses.definition: to appeal to a god or spirit for help, guidance, or protection
senses.definitionCN: 向神灵或精怪求助、求指引或求庇护
senses.example: The sailors invoked the sea god as the storm broke.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴来临时，水手们向海神祈求。
senses.why: Latin invocare joined in- with vocare, to call: the word begins with a voice calling a name outward, and a god answering that call is its oldest scene.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 invocare 由 in- 与 vocare（呼叫）组成：这个词一开始就是一个向外喊出名字的声音，神明应声而来是它最古老的场景。

senses.title: To cite a law, right, or principle
senses.definition: to refer to a law, rule, right, or precedent as the authority for what one does or claims
senses.definitionCN: 引用法律、规则、权利或先例，作为自己行为或主张的依据
senses.example: The union invoked the safety clause in the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 工会援引了合同中的安全条款。
senses.why: A clause cannot be heard, but naming it works like the same call: the speaker summons a rule to stand beside the argument, as if it had been called in.
senses.whyCN: 条款本身不会发声，但把它念出来就是同一个动作：说话人把一条规则召到论据旁边，仿佛它是被喊来的。

senses.title: To bring an image or feeling to mind
senses.definition: to make an image, memory, feeling, or atmosphere appear in the mind or in a place
senses.definitionCN: 使意象、记忆、感受或氛围在脑海中或场景中显现
senses.example: The old port invokes memories of the age of sail.
senses.exampleCN: 这座旧港口让人想起帆船时代。
senses.why: What has been called is now present: the same summoning gesture makes a memory or a mood step forward and fill the scene.
senses.whyCN: 被叫来的东西就出现在场：同一个召唤动作让记忆或情绪走上前来，充满整个场景。

senses.title: To put a rule or power into effect
senses.definition: to use a power, measure, or emergency rule that exists but has been kept ready until now
senses.definitionCN: 动用一项早就备好、此前未启用的权力、措施或紧急规定
senses.example: The governor invoked emergency powers after the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪灾之后，州长启用了紧急权力。
senses.why: A power waits like a sleeper until its name is called; invoking it is the moment the call sets it working.
senses.whyCN: 权力像睡着的人等被叫名字；invoke 的那一刻，就是这一声呼唤让它开始运转。

senses.title: To start a routine in computing
senses.definition: to cause a function, method, or program to run at a chosen point during a program
senses.definitionCN: 在程序的某个位置使函数、方法或程序开始运行
senses.example: The script invokes the backup routine every midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 脚本每天午夜调用备份程序。
senses.why: Programmers kept the old image in a new world: code stays still until another part of the program calls it by name and sets it going.
senses.whyCN: 程序员把旧意象搬进了新世界：代码静静待着，直到程序的另一部分按名字把它叫出来，让它运行。

senses.title: To solemnly call upon someone to act
senses.definition: to call on a person or group, often solemnly, to take part or to explain themselves
senses.definitionCN: 郑重地召唤某人或某群体参与某事，或要求其作出解释
senses.example: Parliament invoked the minister to answer in person.
senses.exampleCN: 议会召唤那位大臣亲自来作答。
senses.why: The oldest layer of the word returns here: a voice calls a person by name and expects an answer, without any god or clause involved.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的层次在这里回归：一个声音点名唤人，并期待回答，既不必涉及神明，也不必涉及条款。

intro.en: Invoke comes from the Latin verb vocare, to call, with the prefix in- added, meaning to call upon.
intro.cn: invoke 来自拉丁语动词 vocare（呼叫），加上前缀 in-，意为「向……呼喊」。

items.en: The voice root is generally reconstructed as *wek-, meaning to speak or call. Its deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 「声音」词根一般认为可重构为 *wek-，表示「说、呼叫」；更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Vocare meant to call or summon, and it also yielded vox, the voice.
items.cn: vocare 意为呼叫、召唤，它还生出 vox，即「声音」。

items.en: The prefix in- plus vocare formed invocare, to call on a god, to appeal to, or to call in for help.
items.cn: in- 与 vocare 构成 invocare，意为祈求神灵、向……求助或召来援助。

items.en: Old French invoker carried the word into English, and the religious sense came with it.
items.cn: 古法语 invoker 把这个词带入英语，宗教含义也随之而来。

items.en: The verb is recorded in English in the fifteenth century with the sense of calling on God; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个动词在十五世纪见于英语，意为呼求上帝；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Law stretched the call to clauses and rights, and computing later stretched it to functions run by name.
items.cn: 法律把「呼喊」扩展到条款与权利，计算机科学后来又扩展到按名字运行的函数。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the same voice root with different prefixes; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for calling on something.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「声音」词根加不同前缀构成的词；近义组收表示「召唤、唤起」的动词。

entries.definition: The grammatical case used when addressing a person directly, as in a form of address.
entries.definitionCN: 语法术语「呼格」，指直接称呼某人时用的格，与本词共享呼叫词根。

entries.definition: To cancel or withdraw a decision, licence, or promise; re- calls it back.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「撤销、撤回」，前缀 re- 表示「回」，把东西叫回来。

entries.definition: To stir up anger or a reaction; pro- calls something forward.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「激起、挑动」，前缀 pro- 表示「向前」，把东西叫出来。

entries.definition: To bring a feeling or memory out; e- calls it out of hiding.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「唤起、引起」，前缀 e- 表示「向外」，把感受叫出来。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of calling on someone or citing something solemnly.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「祈求、援引」，由本词加 -ation 构成。

entries.definition: To mention a law or source as evidence; the plain word for backing an argument with authority.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「引用」，指以法律或资料为依据支持论点，语气平实。

entries.definition: To speak to a god in order to give thanks or ask for help; personal rather than ritual.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「祈祷」，是个人而非仪式性的求助。

entries.definition: To order someone to come, or to gather strength; the act of calling someone in.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「召唤、鼓起」，指命令某人前来或聚集力量。

entries.definition: To turn to a way of acting when nothing else is left; used for a last option.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「诉诸、采用」，多指别无选择时的最后手段。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin call root and the phrases this verb actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的拉丁「呼叫」词根，以及这个动词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Vocare means to call, so invoke is to call something in.
normal.cn: vocare 意为呼叫，所以 invoke 就是把某物叫进来。

normal.en: The family lines up by prefix: invoke, evoke, provoke, revoke.
normal.cn: 这一族词按前缀排队：invoke、evoke、provoke、revoke。

normal.en: Lawyers invoke a clause, and officials invoke emergency powers.
normal.cn: 律师 invoke 条款，官员 invoke 紧急权力。

normal.en: The noun invocation names the calling and the ritual that goes with it.
normal.cn: 名词 invocation 指这一声呼唤，也指与它配套的仪式。

normal.en: Vox, the word for voice, comes from the same root as invoke.
normal.cn: 表示声音的 vox 与 invoke 同出一源。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised toward the sky with a name called out into the wind.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手举向天空，一个名字被喊进风里。

abstract.en: See a heavy book of law opening on its own when a clause is named aloud.
abstract.cn: 想象一本厚重的法典在被念出条款时自己翻开。

abstract.en: Imagine the lights coming on across a dark port as their names are called.
abstract.cn: 想象在暗下来的港口里，名字被叫到一处，灯就亮起一处。

examples.en: The priestess invoked the goddess of the harvest before the sowing.
examples.cn: 播种前，女祭司向丰收女神祈求。

examples.en: Many speakers invoke the principle of fairness without defining it.
examples.cn: 许多演讲者援引公平原则，却并不给它下定义。

examples.en: When the alarm sounds, the system invokes the shutdown procedure.
examples.cn: 警报响起时，系统会调用关机程序。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因沃克」——一声叫唤，那东西因这呼声而到位：召唤、援引

root: 拉丁语 vocare「呼叫」← 一般认为源自原始印欧语 *wek-「说、呼叫」；加前缀 in-「向、进入」构成 invocare「呼求、召来」，经古法语 invoker 进入英语。同族的称呼词根还生出 vox「声音」、vocative「呼格」；换前缀则得 evoke、provoke、revoke。核心意象是「出声把一个名字叫到面前」。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses all describe one act of calling: calling a god first, then a law, then a memory, then a power, then a routine in code, and finally a person who must answer.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项描述的都是同一个「叫」的动作：先叫神灵，再叫法律，叫记忆，叫权力，叫代码里的子程序，最后叫一个必须作答的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a raised hand and a name called outward, answered by what was named.
core.cn: 核心意象：举手的一声呼唤，被叫的名字应声而来。

branches.en: THE GODS: the earliest use is a voice asking the divine for help.
branches.cn: 神灵线：最早的用法是一个声音向上天求助。

branches.en: THE LAW: a named clause or power answers the call and stands behind the speaker.
branches.cn: 法律线：被念出的条款或权力应答而来，站在说话人身后。

branches.en: THE CALLER: a memory arrives, or a person is summoned to answer in the open.
branches.cn: 召唤线：记忆应声而至，或者人被叫到明处作答。

branches.en: THE MACHINE: code sits still until it is called by name, the same gesture in a new world.
branches.cn: 机器线：代码静静待着，直到按名字被叫出，这是同一动作在新世界里的样子。

branches.en: Both calling a god and citing a clause put the speaker in front of a higher authority.
branches.cn: 呼求神灵与援引条款，都把说话人置于更高的权威面前。

intro.en: Invoke is the Latin prefix in- plus the calling root vocare, with -ation making the noun and other prefixes making its siblings.
intro.cn: invoke 是拉丁语前缀 in- 加呼叫词根 vocare，-ation 构成名词，换前缀则得到同族兄弟词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vocare, vox, invocare and invocatio are all recorded forms, so only the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vocare 与 invocare 都有文献记录，vox 与 invocatio 亦然，只有更早的印欧词根属于重构形式。

items.example: The root carries the idea of a voice.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根承载着「声音」的意思。

items.example: The verb is the direct source of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一词族的直接来源。

items.example: Vox is the noun made from the same root.
items.exampleCN: vox 是同根产生的名词。

items.example: The prefix in- points the call toward someone.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 把这声呼喊指向某人。

items.example: The prefix marks the direction of the call.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出呼喊的方向。

items.example: It forms invocation.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 invocation。

items.example: It forms evoke, to call out.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 evoke，即把东西叫出来。

items.example: It forms provoke, to call forward.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 provoke，即把东西向前叫出。

items.example: It forms revoke, to call back.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 revoke，即把东西叫回来。

items.example: It forms vocative in grammar.
items.exampleCN: 它在语法中构成 vocative 呼格。

definition_zh: 碘；碘酊；碘制剂
definition_en: a dark greyish solid element that gives off a violet vapour, and the antiseptic made from it
core_image: 一小块黑紫色晶体在烧瓶里加热，腾起一团紫色的云
scene: 实验台上一只加热的烧瓶，底部躺着几粒发黑的小晶体，火焰一烤，瓶里升起一团紫雾。Warm iodine crystals give off a violet vapour that stains the glass.
sceneCN: 这里 iodine 是「碘」（第 1 个义项：一种会升华的卤族元素）；句意为把碘晶体加热，会冒出紫色的蒸气，在玻璃上留下痕迹。

derivatives.zh: 由词干加 -ide 构成，义为「碘化物」，指与金属等化合成的碘的化合物
由词干加 -ic 构成，义为「碘的；高价碘的」
由本词与质量数构成，义为「碘一三一」，一种用于诊疗的放射性同位素
由词干加 -ization 构成，义为「加碘」，多指在食盐中加碘
由词干加 -metry「测量」构成，义为「碘量法」，一种利用碘的滴定分析法

senses.title: The chemical element
senses.definition: a non-metallic element of the halogen group, a dark greyish solid that sublimates into a violet vapour
senses.definitionCN: 卤族的一种非金属元素，常温下是深灰黑色的固体，会直接升华成紫色蒸气
senses.example: Iodine turns from a solid to a violet gas without becoming liquid.
senses.exampleCN: 碘由固体直接变成紫色气体，中间不经过液态。
senses.why: The French name was coined from the Greek word for violet because of the colour of its vapour; the element is named after the cloud it makes.
senses.whyCN: 法语名称由希腊语「紫罗兰」造出，因为它蒸气呈紫色；这个元素是以它冒出的那团紫色云雾命名的。

senses.title: The antiseptic solution
senses.definition: a brown antiseptic liquid in which iodine is dissolved, swabbed on the skin to kill germs
senses.definitionCN: 把碘溶解其中制成的棕色消毒药水，涂在皮肤上杀菌
senses.example: The nurse dabbed iodine on the cut before bandaging it.
senses.exampleCN: 护士包扎前在伤口上涂了碘酒。
senses.why: Once the element kills germs, the liquid that carries it is simply called by its own name: the substance gives its name to the bottle.
senses.whyCN: 元素既然能杀菌，装它的药水就直接沿用它的名字：物质把自己的名字借给了瓶子。

senses.title: A nutrient that the body needs
senses.definition: the small amount of the element that the body needs to make thyroid hormones
senses.definitionCN: 人体为合成甲状腺激素所必需、需要量很少的那种元素
senses.example: Areas far from the sea often suffer from iodine deficiency.
senses.exampleCN: 远离海洋的地区常常存在缺碘问题。
senses.why: From the element comes the dietary sense: a trace of this purple solid keeps the thyroid working, so doctors speak of enough or too little iodine.
senses.whyCN: 由元素义延伸出营养义：一点点这种紫色固体会让甲状腺正常运转，所以医生会谈碘够不够。

intro.en: Iodine was named in France in the early nineteenth century, after the Greek word for violet, because of its purple vapour.
intro.cn: iodine 于十九世纪初在法国得名，因紫色蒸气而得名于希腊语「紫罗兰」。

items.en: Ion meant violet or violet-coloured, and the small flower was called ion.
items.cn: ion 意为紫罗兰或紫色，那种小花就叫 ion。

items.en: In 1813 the French chemist Joseph Gay-Lussac named the new element iode, from the Greek word for violet, after the colour of its vapour.
items.cn: 1813 年，法国化学家盖-吕萨克根据蒸气的颜色，用希腊语「紫罗兰」为新元素命名为 iode。

items.en: English adopted the French name together with the ending -ine, giving iodine.
items.cn: 英语连同词尾 -ine 一起借入法语名称，写作 iodine。

items.en: The element was first found in seaweed ash in France around 1811, and the medical uses came soon after.
items.cn: 这个元素约在 1811 年首次发现于法国海藻灰中，随后的医疗用途很快出现。

items.en: Iodine entered public health and medicine: iodized salt, chemical tests, and radioactive tracing.
items.cn: 碘走进公共卫生与医学：加碘盐、化学检验与放射性示踪。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the iodine stem; the near-meaning group gathers other halogens, halides and elements of the same field.
note.cn: 形近组收碘词干构成的词；近义组收同类卤素、卤化物与同一领域的元素。

entries.definition: A compound in which iodine is combined with another element, such as that in iodide of potassium.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「碘化物」，指碘与其他元素化合形成的化合物，如碘化钾。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning containing iodine, especially in a higher oxidation state.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「碘的、高价碘的」，指含碘且尤指处于较高氧化态。

entries.definition: To treat with iodine or to add iodine to something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「碘化、加碘」，指用碘处理或往某物里加碘。

entries.definition: The process of adding iodine to a product, most often to table salt.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「加碘」，即往产品中加碘，最常见的是食盐加碘。

entries.definition: The reddish liquid halogen just above iodine in the periodic table, whose name also comes from a smell.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「溴」，是周期表里位于碘上方的红棕色液体卤素，名称也来自气味。

entries.definition: A greenish halogen gas used to disinfect water.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「氯」，一种淡绿色卤素气体，常用于给水消毒。

entries.definition: The name of the chemical family that includes iodine, chlorine, bromine and fluorine.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「卤素」，是包含碘、氯、溴、氟的化学族名。

entries.definition: A substance that kills germs on the skin; iodine solution is one kind of it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「消毒剂」，指在皮肤上杀灭病菌的物质，碘酒是其中一种。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Greek naming of the element and the phrases it actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用这个元素得名的希腊语由来，以及它实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Iodine is named after the violet colour of its vapour: the name is the colour.
normal.cn: iodine 以蒸气的紫色得名：名字本身就是颜色。

normal.en: Iodide is the compound with -ide, while iodine names the element itself.
normal.cn: iodide 是带 -ide 的化合物，iodine 则是元素本身。

normal.en: Iodine deficiency is the phrase used in global health reports, and iodized salt is the usual answer.
normal.cn: iodine deficiency 是全球卫生报告里的说法，通常的应对办法就是加碘盐。

normal.en: In the lab iodine sublimes: it goes from solid straight to vapour, so there is no liquid stage.
normal.cn: 在实验室里碘会升华：从固体直接变成蒸气，中间没有液态阶段。

normal.en: The Greek word ion means violet, and iodine came into English through French.
normal.cn: 希腊语 ion 意为紫罗兰，iodine 是经由法语进入英语的。

abstract.en: Picture a few dark grains in a flask, and a violet cloud rising from them.
abstract.cn: 想象烧瓶底躺着几粒发黑的晶体，一团紫色云雾从它们身上升起。

abstract.en: See a small brown bottle with a glass rod, ready to dab a cut.
abstract.cn: 想象一只棕色小瓶和一根玻璃棒，随时准备给伤口上药。

abstract.en: Imagine a spoon of white salt turning slightly darker as the iodine settles in it.
abstract.cn: 想象一勺白盐在碘落进去之后微微变深。

examples.en: Heating the sample showed that it contained iodine.
examples.cn: 加热样品后可以看出其中含有碘。

examples.en: Some coastal soils are naturally rich in iodine because of sea spray.
examples.cn: 由于海雾吹拂，一些沿海土壤天然富含碘。

examples.en: The clinic offers a simple blood test to check your iodine levels.
examples.cn: 诊所提供一项简单的血液检查，用来检测你的碘水平。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱典」——一瓶紫得发古典味的药水，是家里的消毒常备：碘；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 ion「紫罗兰」+ 法语化学名词尾 iode → 1813 年盖-吕萨克以蒸气颜色命名为 iode，1814 年英语借入时加上词尾 -ine，成为 iodine。词根与「碘」的物质本身无关，而是直接取自「紫色」这一观感；同词干还派生 iodide「碘化物」、iodic「碘的」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses run from the element, to the bottle of antiseptic made from it, to the trace the body needs for its thyroid hormones.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项由元素起头，再到用它制的消毒药水，最后到人体合成甲状腺激素所需的那一点碘。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: dark crystals in a flask send up a violet cloud.
core.cn: 核心意象：烧瓶里的黑色晶体腾起一团紫色云雾。

branches.en: THE ELEMENT: a halogen solid whose vapour gives it its name.
branches.cn: 元素线：一种卤素固体，蒸气给了它名字。

branches.en: THE BOTTLE: the element dissolved as an antiseptic takes its name.
branches.cn: 药瓶线：元素溶解后制成消毒药水，也沿用它的名字。

branches.en: THE BODY: a trace of the element keeps the thyroid working.
branches.cn: 身体线：一点点这种元素让甲状腺正常运转。

branches.en: Both the sea and the table get their iodine from the same natural sources.
branches.cn: 海洋与餐桌上的碘，都来自同一批天然来源。

branches.en: History ties the two: the antiseptic was the first medical use, and later came the dietary need.
branches.cn: 历史把两者连在一起：消毒是最早的医学用途，营养需求是后来才认识到的。

intro.en: Iodine is a coined French scientific term: a Greek colour word plus a chemical ending, later extended by -ide, -ic and -ization.
intro.cn: iodine 是法语造出的科学术语：希腊语颜色词加化学词尾，后来再用 -ide、-ic、-ization 扩展。

latinIntro.en: Iodine has no Latin origin; its stem is a Greek colour word passed through modern French, so there are no Latin cognates to list.
latinIntro.cn: iodine 没有拉丁语来源；它的词干是一个希腊语颜色词，经近代法语借入英语，因此没有拉丁语同源词可列。

items.example: The Greek word names the colour of the vapour.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊语词指的就是蒸气的颜色。

items.example: The French chemist wrote iode.
items.exampleCN: 那位法国化学家写作 iode。

items.example: The suffix made iodine out of the French word.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把法语词变成了 iodine。

items.meaningCN: 由该元素构成的化合物
items.example: It forms iodide.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 iodide。

items.example: It forms iodic.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 iodic。

items.example: It forms iodinate.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 iodinate。

items.example: It forms iodization, as in salt.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 iodization，用于食盐加碘。

items.example: It forms iodometry, a titration method.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 iodometry，一种滴定法。

items.example: The full word is now a household term.
items.exampleCN: 这个完整词如今已是家常用语。

definition_zh: 虹膜；鸢尾花；彩虹女神
definition_en: the coloured circular part of the eye around the pupil; also a flower with sword shaped leaves
core_image: 一圈彩色的环，中心开着一个通往光的小孔
scene: 医生用灯照着眼睛，仔细查看瞳孔周围那一圈深褐色的组织。The doctor shone a light into the eye and looked at the dark ring of the iris around the pupil.
sceneCN: 这里 iris 是「虹膜」（第 1 个义项：眼睛里有颜色的环状部分）；句意：医生用灯照眼睛，查看瞳孔周围那圈深褐色的虹膜。

forms.label: 复数（拉丁式，多用于解剖学）

derivatives.zh: 虹膜炎（iris 加炎症后缀 -itis）
虹彩般的；闪变色光的（取自「彩虹」意象）
复数形式，既指多片虹膜，也指多株鸢尾花

senses.title: The coloured ring of the eye
senses.definition: the round coloured part of the eye that surrounds the black pupil and controls how much light enters
senses.definitionCN: 眼球中环绕黑色瞳孔的有色圆环，能控制进入眼睛的光量
senses.example: Her irises are a pale grey blue.
senses.exampleCN: 她的虹膜是浅灰蓝色。
senses.why: The Greek goddess Iris was the coloured messenger of the rainbow, so physicians gave the coloured ring of the eye her name.
senses.whyCN: 希腊女神伊里斯是彩虹般色彩缤纷的信使，所以医生用她的名字称呼眼球里彩色的环，这就是虹膜的由来。

senses.title: A tall flower with swordlike leaves
senses.definition: a plant with long flat pointed leaves and large showy flowers, often purple, blue, or yellow
senses.definitionCN: 长着扁平尖叶、开大而艳丽花朵的植物，花色多为紫色、蓝色或黄色
senses.example: Yellow irises grow beside the pond.
senses.exampleCN: 黄色的鸢尾长在池塘边。
senses.why: The petals fan out in many colours like a rainbow, so the rainbow speaking name was given to the striking flower too.
senses.whyCN: 鸢尾花瓣层层展开、颜色缤纷如彩虹，于是这个带「彩虹」意味的名字被借给了这种醒目的花。

senses.title: The messenger goddess of the rainbow
senses.definition: in Greek myth, a goddess who carried the messages of the gods and was linked with the rainbow
senses.definitionCN: 希腊神话中为众神传递消息、与彩虹相联系的女神
senses.example: Poets often picture Iris racing along the rainbow.
senses.exampleCN: 诗人们常想象伊里斯沿着彩虹疾行。
senses.why: The rainbow links heaven and earth, so the messenger between gods and people was imagined as a coloured bridge of light.
senses.whyCN: 彩虹连接天与地，所以往返于神与人之间的信使被想象成一道彩色的光桥。

intro.en: Iris comes from Greek Iris, the name of the rainbow goddess and of the rainbow herself.
intro.cn: iris 来自希腊语 Iris，既是彩虹女神的名字，也是「彩虹」这个词。

items.en: Iris is the name of a messenger goddess and also means rainbow.
items.cn: 希腊语 Iris 既是信使女神的名字，也意为彩虹。

items.en: Botanists use iris for a plant whose flowers show rainbow colours.
items.cn: 植物学家用 iris 指花色如彩虹的植物。

items.en: Roman writers take the name over unchanged as iris.
items.cn: 罗马作家照原样借用这个名字，写作 iris。

items.en: English uses the word for the rainbow goddess and the flower.
items.cn: 英语用它指彩虹女神与鸢尾花。

items.en: Anatomy names the coloured ring of the eye iris.
items.cn: 解剖学开始把眼球的有色环状部分称为虹膜。

note.en: Iris is the rainbow word, close in form to iris like words and in meaning to eye and flower words.
note.cn: iris 是「彩虹」之词，形式上接近拼写相近的家族词，意义上接近眼睛与花卉相关的词。

entries.definition: inflammation of the iris
entries.definitionCN: 虹膜炎，与 iris 同根

entries.definition: showing shifting rainbow colours
entries.definitionCN: 闪变彩虹色的，取自同一「彩虹」意象

entries.definition: a hard silvery metal whose salts show many colours
entries.definitionCN: 坚硬的银色金属，其盐类呈现多种颜色

entries.definition: the small dark opening at the centre of the iris
entries.definitionCN: 瞳孔，位于虹膜中央的小黑孔

entries.definition: the band of colours seen in the sky after rain
the coloured part of a plant that produces seed
entries.definitionCN: 花，植物产生种子的彩色部分

normalIntro.en: Iris is the rainbow: the coloured ring in the eye, the rainbow coloured flower, the goddess of the rainbow.
normalIntro.cn: iris 就是彩虹：眼里彩色的环、如彩虹般多彩的花、还有彩虹女神。

normal.en: Remember iris by the rainbow thread that runs through all its senses.
normal.cn: 记住 iris 贯穿所有义项的那条「彩虹」线索。

normal.en: The iris controls light like a camera aperture.
normal.cn: 虹膜像相机光圈一样控制进光量。

normal.en: Iris also names the flower, so one word covers eye and garden.
normal.cn: iris 还指鸢尾花，一个词同时涵盖眼睛与花园。

normal.en: The plural irises is regular, while irides appears in medical writing.
normal.cn: 复数 irises 是常规写法，irides 多出现在医学文本里。

normal.en: Compare pupil: the pupil is the black hole, the iris is the coloured ring.
normal.cn: 对比 pupil：瞳孔是黑色的孔，虹膜是有色的环。

abstract.en: Picture a coloured velvet ring closing and opening in the sun.
abstract.cn: 想象一个彩色丝绒环在阳光下张开又收拢。

abstract.en: Imagine a fan of pointed petals opening like a rainbow.
abstract.cn: 想象几片带尖的花瓣像彩虹一样展开。

abstract.en: See a slender messenger in a rainbow cloak running across the sky.
abstract.cn: 想象一位披着彩虹斗篷的轻盈信使在天空奔走。

examples.en: Light enters the eye through the pupil and passes the iris.
examples.cn: 光线经瞳孔进入眼睛，并穿过虹膜。

examples.en: Irises of many colours line the garden path.
examples.cn: 园中小路两旁开满各色鸢尾。

examples.en: The camera lens works like an iris, opening for dim light.
examples.cn: 相机镜头像虹膜一样工作，在暗处张开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱丽丝」——想到爱丽丝的眼睛里那圈彩色的虹膜；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 Iris（彩虹女神；彩虹）→ 拉丁语 iris → 英语 iris，核心义「彩虹的彩色」。

sensesIntro.en: Iris starts with the mythic rainbow goddess, then colours the eye ring and the flower.
sensesIntro.cn: iris 从神话里的彩虹女神出发，再把「彩虹之色」分别给了眼球的色环与鸢尾花。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coloured ring that opens in the middle, like a rainbow around a hole.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个中间开口的彩色圆环，像套在小孔外的彩虹。

branches.en: The eye ring is the everyday technical sense.
branches.cn: 眼球色环是日常与技术语境中最常用的义项。

branches.en: The flower keeps the rainbow colour image in the garden.
branches.cn: 鸢尾花在花园里延续了彩虹色这一意象。

branches.en: The goddess supplies the original mythic source.
branches.cn: 女神义项是这个词最初的神话来源。

branches.en: The eye ring was named after the rainbow goddess.
branches.cn: 眼球色环正是得名于彩虹女神。

branches.en: Both flower and goddess are tied to the rainbow.
branches.cn: 鸢尾花与彩虹女神都与彩虹相连。

intro.en: Iris is a whole borrowed name, with no English prefix or suffix; the family grows from the Greek root irid meaning rainbow.
intro.cn: iris 是整体借来的专名，没有英语前缀或后缀；词族从希腊语词根 irid（彩虹）生长出来。

latinIntro.en: Latin iris, taken from Greek, means rainbow and the goddess of the rainbow.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 iris 借自希腊语，意为彩虹与彩虹女神。

items.example: Greek iris carries the rainbow image.
items.exampleCN: 希腊语 iris 带着彩虹意象。

items.meaning: of the iris of the eye
items.meaningCN: 与眼球虹膜有关的构词成分
items.example: The combining form irid appears in medical words.
items.exampleCN: 构词成分 irid 出现在医学词汇中。

items.example: The suffix -itis makes iritis.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -itis 构成 iritis（虹膜炎）。

items.meaningCN: 呈现……的；逐渐变成……的词尾
items.example: The suffix -escent helps form iridescent.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -escent 帮助构成 iridescent。

items.example: Iridescent pearl shells catch light in shifting colours.
items.exampleCN: 虹彩般的珍珠贝壳在光下变换颜色。

items.example: Iritis makes the eye red and painful.
items.exampleCN: 虹膜炎使眼睛发红疼痛。

items.example: The suffix -ium builds iridium.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ium 构成 iridium。

items.example: Iridium salts glow in many rainbow colours.
items.exampleCN: 铱的盐类散发着彩虹般的多种颜色。

items.example: The suffix -es makes irises.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -es 构成 irises。

definition_zh: 反讽；讽刺；出人意料的局面
definition_en: the use of words to mean the opposite of what they appear to say, or a situation that seems the reverse of what is expected
core_image: 一个人嘴上一本正经，眼里却带着相反的意思
scene: 他说那场暴雨真是个好天气，脸上写满了无奈。He said the downpour was lovely weather, and his tone was pure irony.
sceneCN: 这里 irony 是「反讽」（第 1 个义项：说的和想的正好相反）；句意：他说这场暴雨是好天气，语气里满是反讽。

pos.zh: 反讽；讽刺；出人意料的局面

collocations.zh: 讽刺地；具有讽刺意味的是

derivatives.zh: 反讽的；讽刺的（irony 加形容词后缀 -ic）
具有讽刺意味地（ironic 加副词后缀 -ally）
用反讽的方式说或写（较少见，irony 加动词后缀 -ize）

senses.title: Saying the opposite of what is meant
senses.definition: the use of words that say one thing while meaning the opposite, usually to be humorous or critical
senses.definitionCN: 表面说一件事而实际表达相反意思的说话方式，多用于幽默或批评
senses.example: Her praise was irony, and everyone knew it.
senses.exampleCN: 她的赞美是反话，谁都听得出来。
senses.why: In Greek comedy the eiron was a smooth talker who hid what he meant, so the word means a pretending speaker.
senses.whyCN: 希腊喜剧里的 eiron 是表面平静、藏起真实想法的角色，所以这个词本义就是「假装的人」。

senses.title: A gap between what is expected and what happens
senses.definition: a situation that seems the opposite of what would be expected or suitable
senses.definitionCN: 与预期或情理相反的处境
senses.example: The irony is that the safety expert got hurt at home.
senses.exampleCN: 讽刺的是，那位安全专家竟在家里受了伤。
senses.why: From pretending words the word moved to events that behave like a pretender, hiding a mocking gap between plan and outcome.
senses.whyCN: 从「装着说的词」扩展到像假装者一样的事件，在计划与结果之间藏着一个嘲弄人的落差。

senses.title: A gap in knowledge between characters and audience
senses.definition: a dramatic effect in which the audience knows something that a character on stage does not
senses.definitionCN: 观众知道舞台上人物尚不知情的戏剧手法
senses.example: The irony deepens when he greets his killer as a friend.
senses.exampleCN: 当他称呼杀手为朋友时，这种反讽加深了。
senses.why: Stage audience and actor hold different knowledge, and that visible gap turns the word pretending scene into a technique.
senses.whyCN: 观众与演员掌握的信息不同，这个看得见的落差把「假装」的场景变成了一种戏剧技巧。

senses.title: A mocking tone in literature
senses.definition: harmless seeming remarks used in fiction or speech to mock a person or idea
senses.definitionCN: 在小说或言谈中以看似无害的话语嘲弄人物或想法
senses.example: Swift uses irony to attack greedy officials.
senses.exampleCN: 斯威夫特用嘲讽笔调抨击贪婪的官员。
senses.why: When the pretending speaker writes, the hidden opposite becomes a tool for satirists and novelists.
senses.whyCN: 当「假装的人」开始写作，藏起来的相反意思就成了讽刺作家与小说家的工具。

senses.title: The quality of being ironic
senses.definition: the noticeable force or flavour of words and events that seem to mock themselves
senses.definitionCN: 言语或事件显得自我嘲弄的那种意味或力道
senses.example: The old factory museum still smells of irony.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧厂房博物馆仍透着讽刺意味。
senses.why: Speakers soon talk about irony as a quality that words and objects can share, not only as a single act of pretending.
senses.whyCN: 人们很快把反讽说成言语和事物共有的一种特质，而不只是一次假装。

intro.en: Irony comes from Greek eironeia, pretending or dissembling, through Latin ironia.
intro.cn: irony 来自希腊语 eironeia（假装、掩饰），经拉丁语 ironia 进入英语。

items.en: Eironeia means pretending not to know or to mean something.
items.cn: 希腊语 eironeia 意为假装不知情或假装无意表达某意。

items.en: In comedy the eiron is the understated character who wins by pretending.
items.cn: 希腊喜剧里，eiron 是靠假装而占上风、说话含蓄的角色。

items.en: Latin ironia keeps the sense of dissimulation in rhetoric.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ironia 保留修辞中「掩饰真意」的含义。

items.en: English adopts irony first as a figure of speech.
items.cn: 英语最初把 irony 当作一种修辞格吸收进来。

items.en: The sense widens to events that mock expectation.
items.cn: 这个词的含义扩展到嘲弄人们预期的事件。

note.en: Irony is the root of ironic and ironically, and it stands near satire, sarcasm, and paradox in meaning.
note.cn: irony 是 ironic 与 ironically 的词根，意义上靠近 satire、sarcasm 与 paradox。

entries.definition: showing irony
in an ironic way
entries.definitionCN: 讽刺地；具有讽刺意味地

entries.definition: to speak or write with irony
entries.definitionCN: 以反讽的方式说或写，较少见

entries.definition: sharp mocking words meant to hurt
entries.definitionCN: 尖刻的讽刺话，意在伤人

entries.definition: writing that uses humour to expose faults
entries.definitionCN: 用幽默揭露缺点的写作形式

entries.definition: a statement that seems self contradictory yet may be true
entries.definitionCN: 看似自相矛盾却可能成立的说法

normalIntro.en: Irony is a mask: the face says one thing and the voice carries the opposite.
normalIntro.cn: irony 是一张面具：脸上的话一套，语气里却是另一套。

normal.en: Remember that irony names the pretending speaker of Greek comedy, the eiron.
normal.cn: 记住 irony 源自希腊喜剧里那个装傻的说话人 eiron。

normal.en: Tone of irony is often heard in praise that hides blame.
normal.cn: 反讽的语气常出现在暗藏责备的称赞里。

normal.en: The irony of fate describes events that mock our plans.
normal.cn: the irony of fate 描述嘲弄我们计划的事件。

normal.en: Dramatic irony puts the audience ahead of the character.
normal.cn: 戏剧性反讽让观众比人物先知道真相。

normal.en: Compare sarcasm: sarcasm cuts, irony only flips the meaning.
normal.cn: 对比 sarcasm：sarcasm 是要伤人，irony 主要是把意思翻转过来。

abstract.en: Hear a voice say one thing while the eyebrows say the reverse.
abstract.cn: 想象一张嘴说着一套，眉毛却在说相反的。

abstract.en: See a firefighter whose own house burns down.
abstract.cn: 想象一位消防员的自家房子反倒着了火。

abstract.en: Picture an audience holding a secret the hero cannot see.
abstract.cn: 想象观众握着一个主角看不见的秘密。

examples.en: There is a bitter irony in a doctor who fears hospitals.
examples.cn: 一位害怕医院的医生身上带着苦涩的反讽。

examples.en: The irony of the plan was that it saved the very thing it meant to destroy.
examples.cn: 这个计划的讽刺之处在于，它反倒保全了它想摧毁的东西。

examples.en: Dramatic irony makes the final scene unbearable to watch.
examples.cn: 戏剧性反讽让最后一幕令人不忍观看。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱若你」——嘴上说「爱若你」，心里却冷笑着，正是反话。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 eironeia（假装、掩饰；喜剧角色 eiron）→ 拉丁语 ironia → 英语 irony，核心义「表面一套、内里一层」。

sensesIntro.en: Irony moves from a pretending speaker through situational and dramatic gaps to a general mocking flavour.
sensesIntro.cn: irony 从「假装的说话人」出发，经历情境落差与戏剧落差，最后成为一种普遍的嘲讽意味。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a smooth mask on a face that hides the opposite of its words.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张光滑的面具戴在脸上，藏住与话语相反的意思。

branches.en: The verbal sense is the oldest and most familiar.
branches.cn: 言语反讽是最古老、最熟悉的义项。

branches.en: A situation can act like a pretender too.
branches.cn: 情境本身也可以像假装者一样嘲弄人。

branches.en: Drama turns the gap between knowers into a device.
branches.cn: 戏剧把知情落差变成了一种手法。

branches.en: Literature and everyday talk keep irony as a flavour.
branches.cn: 文学与日常言谈把反讽保留为一种意味。

branches.en: Words, events, and writing all share the flipped meaning.
branches.cn: 话语、事件与文字共享「意思翻转」这一核心。

intro.en: Irony is built from Greek eiron plus the abstract suffix -eia; English forms ironic and ironically from the stem iron.
intro.cn: irony 由希腊语 eiron 加抽象词尾 -eia 构成；英语用词干 iron 造出 ironic 与 ironically。

latinIntro.en: Latin ironia, borrowed from Greek, means irony or dissimulation in speech.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ironia 借自希腊语，意为言语中的反讽或掩饰。

items.example: Greek eironeia gives the pretending image.
items.exampleCN: 希腊语 eironeia 提供「假装」的意象。

items.meaning: a pretend ignorant character in comedy
items.example: The eiron wins by seeming to know less.
items.exampleCN: eiron 靠显得懂得少而取胜。

items.meaningCN: 表示抽象状态的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -eia builds abstract nouns.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -eia 构成抽象名词。

items.example: The suffix -ic makes ironic.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 构成 ironic。

items.example: An ironic smile showed she did not mean it.
items.exampleCN: 一个反讽的微笑说明她并非真心。

items.example: The suffix -ally makes ironically.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ally 构成 ironically。

items.example: Ironically, the alarm failed first.
items.exampleCN: 讽刺的是，警报器最先失灵。

items.example: The suffix -ize forms ironize from the stem iron.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ize 由词干 iron 构成 ironize。

definition_zh: 不规则；不规律；不规则之处
definition_en: the quality of not following a usual pattern or rule, or an instance of this
core_image: 一排整齐的砖里，突然有几块歪着摆放
scene: 审计员一页页核对手册，很快就盯上了那几笔异常的转账。The auditor checked the ledger and quickly noticed a few irregularities in the payments.
sceneCN: 这里 irregularity 是「违规之处、异常之处」（第 3 个义项：不合规范的做法）；句意：审计员核对账本，很快注意到几笔异常付款。

pos.zh: 不规则；不规律；不规则之处

derivatives.zh: 不规则的（ir- 否定前缀 + regular）
不规则地（irregular 加副词词尾 -ly）
规律性；正规（去掉否定前缀 ir- 的肯定形式）
使合乎规范（regular 加动词词尾 -ize）

senses.title: The quality of not being even or regular
senses.definition: the quality of having an uneven shape, spacing, or surface
senses.definitionCN: 在形状、间距或表面上不均匀的性质
senses.example: Workers sanded the irregularity out of the stone.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们把石头表面的不平处磨平了。
senses.why: The negative prefix ir- denies the Latin rule word regula, so the noun names the plain fact that a shape breaks evenness.
senses.whyCN: 否定前缀 ir- 否定了拉丁语的「规则」之词 regula，所以这个词最直接地表示形状破坏了均匀。

senses.title: A lack of steady timing or pattern
senses.definition: the fact of happening or repeating at uneven or unpredictable times
senses.definitionCN: 发生或重复的时间不均衡、难以预料
senses.example: The irregularity of the buses frustrates commuters.
senses.exampleCN: 公交班次不规律，让通勤者很头疼。
senses.why: From uneven shape the word slides to uneven timing, because a timetable is also a straight line of regular marks.
senses.whyCN: 由空间上的不均滑向时间上的不均，因为时刻表也同样是一排整齐的标记。

senses.title: An act that breaks official rules
senses.definition: a failure to follow official rules, especially in money or public business
senses.definitionCN: 违反官方规定的行为，尤指财务或公务方面
senses.example: The board found several irregularities in the accounts.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会发现账目中有几处违规。
senses.why: A regula is a rule as well as a line, so breaking the line becomes breaking a rule.
senses.whyCN: regula 既是「直线」又是「规章」，于是划出线外的歪斜就成了违规。

senses.title: A form that does not follow the usual rule
senses.definition: a word form or other unit that departs from the usual grammatical pattern
senses.definitionCN: 偏离通常语法规律的形式，如不规则词形
senses.example: Grammar books list the plural irregularity of this noun.
senses.exampleCN: 语法书列出了这个名词的不规则复数形式。
senses.why: Language has its own rules, so a form that steps outside them suffers the same name as any other break.
senses.whyCN: 语言自有一套规则，偏离规则的形态便和别的偏离用同一个名字。

senses.title: Physical variation from the normal
senses.definition: a variation in body function or rhythm that differs from what is normal
senses.definitionCN: 身体机能或节律偏离正常状态的差异
senses.example: Doctors recorded an irregularity in her heartbeat.
senses.exampleCN: 医生记录到她心跳有异常。
senses.why: When the body runs out of step with its usual rhythm, the unevenness turns medical and the word quietly drops its negative charge.
senses.whyCN: 当身体脱离惯常的节律，这种「不齐」就转入医学语境，词义也变得中性。

intro.en: Irregularity joins the negative prefix ir- to the Latin word regular, both from Latin regula, a straight bar or rule.
intro.cn: irregularity 由否定前缀 ir- 加 regular 构成，二者都可追溯到拉丁语 regula（直尺、规则）。

items.en: Regula means a straight rod or bar used for measuring.
items.cn: 拉丁语 regula 意为用来量直的直杆或直尺。

items.en: By extension regula means a rule or a standard of conduct.
items.cn: 由此引申，regula 也指规则或行为规范。

items.en: Regularis means belonging to a rule or a religious order.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 regularis 意为属于规章或教会的修会的。

items.en: Regular enters English meaning according to rule.
items.cn: 中古英语中 regular 进入英语，意为「合乎规则的」。

items.en: Irregularity is used for uneven shapes, wording, and later official misconduct.
items.cn: 英语用 irregularity 表示形状不匀、措辞不规，后来又指公务上的违规。

note.en: Irregularity is the negated noun of regular, next to regularity, anomalous, and misconduct words.
note.cn: irregularity 是 regular 的否定名词，与 regularity、anomaly，以及表示违规的词相邻。

entries.definition: not following the usual rule or pattern
the quality of being even and orderly
entries.definitionCN: 规律性；整齐，是去掉否定前缀的肯定形式

entries.definition: in an uneven or unsteady way
something that differs from the normal pattern
a feature that departs from what is normal
the state of not matching or agreeing

normalIntro.en: Irregularity is the rule book with a bent ruler laid across it: something does not lie straight.
normalIntro.cn: irregularity 像一把弯了的尺子横在规则手册上：有东西没能摆直。

normal.en: Remember ir- as a negative prefix and regula as the Latin rule word.
normal.cn: 记住 ir- 是否定前缀，regula 是拉丁语的「规则」之词。

normal.en: The plural irregularities most often appears in audit and safety reports.
normal.cn: 复数 irregularities 常出现在审计与安全报告中。

normal.en: Medical writing uses irregularity for a rhythm that breaks its pattern.
normal.cn: 医学文献用 irregularity 表示打破节律的不齐。

normal.en: Compare regularity: the same noun with and without the negative prefix.
normal.cn: 对比 regularity：同一个名词，加与不加否定前缀。

normal.en: Regular, regularis, and regularize all keep the straight rule image.
normal.cn: regular、regularis 与 regularize 都保留「直尺与规则」的意象。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler lying at an angle on a ruled notebook page.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子斜放在画好横线的笔记本页面上。

abstract.en: Hear a bus timetable where some times are missing.
abstract.cn: 想象一张时刻表上有些时点被抹掉了。

abstract.en: See a page of accounts with one figure circled in red.
abstract.cn: 想象一页账目上有一个数字被红笔圈了出来。

examples.en: The inspector blamed the crash on an irregularity in the brakes.
examples.cn: 检查员把这次碰撞归咎于刹车系统的一处异常。

examples.en: Irregularities in the voting records led to a recount.
examples.cn: 投票记录中的违规之处引发了重新计票。

examples.en: A slight irregularity in the shape does not matter.
examples.cn: 形状上的一点不规则并无大碍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一瑞哥来瑞提」——一列队伍里有个「瑞哥」老是歪着站，队伍就不整齐了。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ir-（否定）+ regularis（合乎规章的）← regula（直尺；规则）+ -ity → 英语 irregularity，核心义「偏离直线与规则」。

sensesIntro.en: Irregularity begins with uneven shape, moves to uneven timing, and then to broken rules, broken forms, and medical variation.
sensesIntro.cn: irregularity 先指形状不匀，再指时间不规律，随后延伸为违规、不合规则的形式与生理异常。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a few bricks in a straight wall that sit askew.
core.cn: 核心意象：一堵笔直的砖墙里有几块砖歪着。

branches.en: The physical sense is the most literal.
branches.cn: 物理层面的不匀是最字面的义项。

branches.en: Timing becomes the next place where evenness fails.
branches.cn: 时间成为下一个失去规律性的领域。

branches.en: Rules and bodies both register departures from standard.
branches.cn: 规章与身体都在记录对标准的偏离。

branches.en: Grammar has rules of its own, so forms can be irregular.
branches.cn: 语法自有规则，所以词形也会不合规则。

branches.en: All three senses answer the question of what happened versus what should happen.
branches.cn: 这三个义项都在回答「实际发生了什么」与「本该怎样」之间的差异。

intro.en: Irregularity carries the negative prefix ir- and the noun suffix -ity, built on the Latin rule word regula.
intro.cn: irregularity 带有否定前缀 ir- 与名词词尾 -ity，建立在拉丁语「规则」之词 regula 上。

latinIntro.en: Latin regula means a straight ruler and also a rule, giving regularis and the later English family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 regula 意为直尺，也指规章，由此生出 regularis 与后来的英语词族。

items.example: The prefix ir- turns regular into irregular.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ir- 把 regular 变成 irregular。

items.example: Regula gives the straight line image.
items.exampleCN: regula 提供直线的意象。

items.example: Regularis leads to English regular.
items.exampleCN: regularis 引出英语 regular。

items.example: Regular visits keep the site safe.
items.exampleCN: 定期巡查能保证场地安全。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ity forms irregularity from regular.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 由 regular 构成 irregularity。

items.meaning: not even or not according to rule
items.example: An irregular verb has an old form.
items.exampleCN: 不规则动词带有古老的形态。

items.example: The suffix -ly makes irregularly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 irregularly。

items.example: The suffix -ize forms regularize.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ize 构成 regularize。

definition_zh: 不相关的；不相干的；无关紧要的；不合适宜的
definition_en: not connected with the matter being discussed or dealt with
core_image: 一张答题卡，答案写在另一道题的格子里
scene: 组会上有人先要大家汇报各自的选题，导师打断他，提醒先不要扯别的，说明当前这次讨论的话题。In this group meeting the supervisor asked everyone to stay on the topic and not to raise anything irrelevant.
sceneCN: 这里 irrelevant 是「不相关的」（第 1 个义项：与当前话题没有关联）；句意：组会上导师让大家紧扣主题，不要提出不相关的事情。

pos.zh: 不相关的；不相干的；离题的

derivatives.zh: 无关；不相干；边角题外话
不相关地；离题地
相关的；切题的
相关性；关联度

senses.title: Not connected with the subject
senses.definition: having no connection with what is being discussed or considered
senses.definitionCN: 与正在讨论或考虑的内容没有关联
senses.example: A remark about the weather is irrelevant to a meeting about next year budget.
senses.exampleCN: 在讨论明年预算的会议上聊天气，是离题的话。
senses.why: The prefix in- means not, and relevant means connected to the matter, so irrelevant is literally not related to it.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 in- 表示「不」，relevant 表示「与某事有关」，所以 irrelevant 字面上就是「与之无关」。

senses.title: Of no practical importance
senses.titleCN: 无关紧要的；无足轻重的
senses.definition: not important enough to affect a decision or a result
senses.definitionCN: 重要程度不足以影响决定或结果
senses.example: At that late hour, the price of the ticket was irrelevant.
senses.exampleCN: 到了那么晚的时候，票价已经无关紧要了。
senses.why: From not connected, the meaning widens from the topic to the decision, so something that cannot change an outcome becomes irrelevant.
senses.whyCN: 从「与话题无关」扩展到「与决定无关」：一件改变不了结果的事，就成了无关紧要的事。

senses.title: Out of place in the situation
senses.definition: not suitable for the particular situation and therefore awkward
senses.definitionCN: 与具体场合不相称，因而显得尴尬突兀
senses.example: His joke about money seemed irrelevant during the quiet ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 在肃静的仪式上，他那个关于钱的玩笑显得很不合时宜。
senses.why: When a remark misses the situation as well as the topic, people feel it is not just off-topic but out of place.
senses.whyCN: 一句话既偏离话题又不符合场合时，人们会觉得它不仅仅是离题，更是格格不入。

senses.title: No longer useful or current
senses.definition: no longer useful, needed, or up to date in a changing setting
senses.definitionCN: 在不断变化的环境中不再有用、不再被需要或不再适用
senses.example: Once the software updated itself, the old manual became irrelevant.
senses.exampleCN: 软件自动更新之后，那本旧手册就派不上用场了。
senses.why: Time makes connections turn stale: when no part of a job depends on something any more, it drops out and becomes irrelevant.
senses.whyCN: 时间让联系变旧：当一项工作中没有任何环节再依赖它时，它就脱落下来，变得不再有用。

intro.en: Irrelevant is a late product of Latin roots: in- means not, re- means back, and levare means to raise, so relevant means raising something up to the point in question.
intro.cn: irrelevant 是较晚由拉丁词根组合而成的词：in- 表示「不」，re- 表示「回」，levare 表示「举起」，所以 relevant 是把东西举到有关的那一点上。

items.en: Levare means to lift or lighten, and relevare means to raise up or relieve.
items.cn: levare 意为举起、减轻，relevare 意为抬起或减轻负担。

items.en: The participle relevans, meaning raising up, is the direct base of the later adjective.
items.cn: 分词 relevans（抬起、举起）是后来形容词的直接基础。

items.en: Relevant appears in English, first in legal and administrative writing, with the sense of bearing on the case at hand.
items.cn: relevant 进入英语，起初多见于法律与行政文书，指与手头案件有关。

items.en: The negative in- yields irrelevant, formed much later and only slowly fixed in dictionaries.
items.cn: 否定前缀 in- 造出 irrelevant，这一形式形成得晚得多，词典里的写法也经过缓慢定型。

items.en: In modern English irrelevant covers not only topics and documents but also things out of date.
items.cn: 在现代英语中，irrelevant 不仅指话题和文件，也指过时无用的东西。

note.en: Irrelevant is the negative of relevant; its neighbours are the root family and words for being off the point.
note.cn: irrelevant 是 relevant 的否定形式；它的近邻既有同根词族，也有表示「不切题」的词。

entries.definition: connected with the matter at hand
entries.definitionCN: 与手头事情相关的（正是去掉否定前缀后的原词）

entries.definition: the state of being unrelated to the matter
entries.definitionCN: 无关；不相干（形容词加名词后缀 -ance）

entries.definition: in a way that is not connected with the point
entries.definitionCN: 离题地；不相关地（加副词后缀 -ly）

entries.definition: not important for the question being decided
entries.definitionCN: 无关紧要的；不重要（与材料、物质无关）

entries.definition: having no connection with something else
not relevant to the subject under discussion
entries.definitionCN: 离题的；不切题的（固定短语）

normalIntro.en: Irrelevant is built from a clear frame: in- says not, and relevant says tied to the point.
normalIntro.cn: irrelevant 的构词框架很清楚：in- 说「不」，relevant 说「与要点相连」。

normal.en: The prefix in- before an r often turns into ir-, as in irregular and irresponsible.
normal.cn: 前缀 in- 后接字母 r 时常常写成 ir-，如 irregular 与 irresponsible。

normal.en: The opposite is relevant, so keep the pair on one card.
normal.cn: 它的反义词是 relevant，把这对词放在一张卡片上记。

normal.en: The pattern is be relevant to, so learn it as irrelevant to as well.
normal.cn: 常用结构是 be relevant to，因此也一并记住 irrelevant to。

normal.en: The noun irrelevance and the adverb irrelevantly keep the same block.
normal.cn: 名词 irrelevance 和副词 irrelevantly 沿用同一词块，只需更换后缀。

normal.en: In exam writing, replacing irrelevant details with concrete evidence lifts the score.
normal.cn: 在考试写作中，用具体的证据替代无关的细节能提分。

abstract.en: Picture an answer written in the box of a different question.
abstract.cn: 想象一个答案被写在了另一道题的答题格里。

abstract.en: Picture a price tag on a ticket at the gate, long after it can change any choice.
abstract.cn: 想象检票口前一张再也影响不了选择的票价标签。

abstract.en: Picture a joke told at the worst possible moment of a quiet ceremony.
abstract.cn: 想象在肃静的仪式上最不该讲笑话的时刻讲了一个笑话。

examples.en: The budget cut is irrelevant to the delay in the project.
examples.cn: 削减预算与这个项目的延误无关。

examples.en: Please keep the report short and cut every irrelevant detail.
examples.cn: 请把报告写短，删去所有无关的细节。

examples.en: His personal opinions are irrelevant to the quality of the research.
examples.cn: 他的个人看法与这项研究的质量无关。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「唉，relate 不」——想「唉，跟这事 relate（关联）不上」，就是不相干。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ re-（回）+ levare（举起）→ relevare（抬起）→ relevant（与问题相连的）→ 加否定前缀 in-（在 r 前变 ir-）→ irrelevant，核心义「没有挂到问题上去」。

sensesIntro.en: Irrelevant starts with being off the topic, widens to being unimportant for a decision, then becomes out of place in a setting, and finally outdated.
sensesIntro.cn: irrelevant 先指偏离话题，再扩展到对决定无关紧要，继而指与场合不相称，最后指过时失效。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an answer that sits in the wrong box on a test sheet.
core.cn: 核心意象：答题卡上一个答案写进了错误题目的格子里。

branches.en: The literal sense: not tied to the point under discussion.
branches.cn: 字面义：与讨论的要点没有挂上联系。

branches.en: Unimportant to a decision is the practical sense.
branches.cn: 对决定不重要，是实用层面的义项。

branches.en: Out of place adds a note of social awkwardness.
branches.cn: 不合时宜增添了社交上的尴尬色彩。

branches.en: Something that fails to connect fades into being of little importance.
branches.cn: 没能挂上联系的东西，会渐渐变得无关紧要。

branches.en: A connection lost over time turns a useful thing into an outdated one.
branches.cn: 随时间失去联系，有用的东西就变成了过时的东西。

intro.en: Irrelevant combines the negative prefix in- (written ir- before r) with relevant, which is built on the Latin stem lev- meaning to raise.
intro.cn: irrelevant 由否定前缀 in-（在 r 前写作 ir-）与 relevant 组合而成，relevant 又建立在拉丁词干 lev-（举起）之上。

latinIntro.en: Latin levare means to lift, the verb relevare means to raise up, and the participle relevans lies behind relevant.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 levare 意为举起，表示抬起的形式形成 relevant 的基础，分词 relevans 是直接来源。

items.example: In- negates the base adjective.
items.exampleCN: in- 把基础形容词变成否定。

items.meaningCN: 不（接在 r 前时的拼写变体）
items.example: Ir- appears before r, as in irrelevant.
items.exampleCN: ir- 出现在 r 前，如 irrelevant。

definition_zh: 无法抗拒的；不可抵抗的；诱人的；令人着迷的
definition_en: too strong or too attractive to be resisted
core_image: 一块刚出炉的巧克力蛋糕摆在一个空肚子的孩子面前
scene: 朋友刚端出烤好的蛋糕，香气飘满整间屋子，她一边伸手去拿一边笑说自己实在忍不住了。She laughed and said the smell made the cake completely irresistible to her.
sceneCN: 这里 irresistible 是「无法抗拒的、太诱人的」（第 1 个义项：因魅力太强而忍不住）；句意：她笑着说蛋糕的香味让她完全没法抗拒。

senses.title: Too tempting to refuse
senses.titleCN: 令人无法抗拒的；太诱人的
senses.definition: so attractive or appealing that it is very hard to say no
senses.definitionCN: 吸引力极强，让人很难拒绝
senses.example: The discount shop caught tourists with an offer that was hard to refuse.
senses.exampleCN: 这家折扣店用一个让人难以拒绝的报价吸引了游客。
senses.why: The word denies resistance, and when the pressure comes from attraction rather than force, irresistible simply means too tempting to refuse.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本身否定「抵抗」，当压力来自吸引力而非强权时，irresistible 就自然表示「太诱人而无法拒绝」。

senses.title: Too strong to be opposed
senses.titleCN: 不可抵抗的；无法抵挡的（力量）
senses.definition: so powerful in force or pressure that opposing it is impossible
senses.definitionCN: 力量或压力强大到无从对抗
senses.example: The old dam finally gave way to the irresistible force of the river.
senses.exampleCN: 老水坝最终被河水那股不可抗拒的力量冲垮了。
senses.why: The literal base is resist, so the word first denies the act of standing against force, as in an irresistible army or flood.
senses.whyCN: 字面基础是 resist（抵抗），所以这个词首先否定「对抗」这个动作，用于军队或洪水时就是势不可挡。

senses.title: Charge with strong feeling
senses.titleCN: 极具感染力的；无法忽视的
senses.definition: having a personal charm or energy that draws people in and cannot be ignored
senses.definitionCN: 带着强烈的个人魅力或气势，令人无法忽视
senses.example: Her smile was so warm that people spoke of an irresistible ease about her.
senses.exampleCN: 她的笑容非常温暖，人们都说她身上有种让人无法抗拒的从容。
senses.why: When charm replaces force, the same frame moves from physical pressure to emotional pull that a person radiates.
senses.whyCN: 当「力」换成「魅力」，同一框架就从物理压力转向一个人散发出的情绪吸引力。

senses.title: Beyond control when it comes to habits
senses.definition: unable to be checked, said of a feeling, urge, or habit
senses.definitionCN: 形容情绪、冲动或习惯时，表示克制不住
senses.example: He felt an irresistible urge to check his phone every few minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 他每隔几分钟就有一股抑制不住的冲动想去看手机。
senses.why: Inside a person, resistance means self-control, so an irresistible urge is a desire that a will cannot stop.
senses.whyCN: 在人的内心，「抵抗」其实就是自控力，所以 irresistible urge 就是意志压不住的欲望。

intro.en: Irresistible is built from the negative in-, the verb resist, and the adjective suffix -ible; resist itself comes from Latin re-, meaning back, and sistere, meaning to stand.
intro.cn: irresistible 由否定前缀 in-、动词 resist 与形容词后缀 -ible 构成；resist 本身源自拉丁语 re-（向后）与 sistere（站立）。

items.en: Sistere means to stand still or to place, and resistere means to stand back, hold out, or oppose.
items.cn: sistere 意为站住、设立，resistere 意为站住脚、顶住或抵挡。

items.en: Old French resister carries the sense of standing against an enemy.
items.cn: 古法语 resister 带着对抗敌人的意味。

items.en: Resist enters English as a verb meaning to withstand or oppose.
items.cn: resist 作为动词进入英语，意为顶住、反抗。

items.en: The negative in- plus resist plus -ible forms irresistible, literally not able to be resisted.
items.cn: 否定前缀 in- 加 resist 再加 -ible 造出 irresistible，字面就是「不能被抵抗的」。

items.en: Modern English extends the word from force and armies to charm, offers, and personal desires.
items.cn: 现代英语把它的用法从武力与军队扩展到魅力、优惠报价和个人欲望。

note.en: Irresistible denies resistance; nearby words cover the root family of resist and the broader field of attraction.
note.cn: irresistible 是「不可抵抗」；相邻的词既有 resist 的词族，也有表示吸引力的词。

entries.definition: to oppose or refuse to accept something
entries.definitionCN: 抵抗；抵制（构词的核心动词）

entries.definition: able to withstand something
the act of opposing or the capacity to withstand
attractive in a way that makes one want it
entries.definitionCN: 诱人的；有吸引力的（偏重于勾起欲望）

entries.definition: so persuasive that one accepts it
entries.definitionCN: 有说服力的（面对的是判断而非欲望）

entries.definition: offering no resistance, rarely used for attraction
entries.definitionCN: 无抵抗力的；不加抵抗的（注意与目标词方向不同）

normalIntro.en: Irresistible is a chain of three pieces: in- not, resist to stand against, and -ible able to be.
normalIntro.cn: irresistible 是三段链：in-（不）加 resist（顶住）加 -ible（能够被……的）。

normal.en: Split the word as ir plus resist plus ible, and the meaning reads itself.
normal.cn: 把词拆成 ir 加 resist 加 ible，意思自己就显露出来了。

normal.en: The base resist contains sistere, to stand, so resisting is standing your ground.
normal.cn: 基础词 resist 含 sistere（站），所以抵抗就是站在原地不退。

normal.en: The suffix -ible is the same as in visible and possible, meaning able to be.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ible 与 visible、possible 中的相同，表示「能够被……的」。

normal.en: The common frame is be irresistible to someone.
normal.cn: 最常用的结构是 be irresistible to someone（对某人难以抗拒）。

normal.en: Note that -ible, not -able, is the spelling after resist.
normal.cn: 注意拼写：resist 之后接的是 -ible，而不是 -able。

abstract.en: Picture a warm chocolate cake on the table while you are still hungry.
abstract.cn: 想象一块热乎的巧克力蛋糕放在桌上，而你正饿着肚子。

abstract.en: Picture a river pushing slowly at a cracked stone wall until it gives way.
abstract.cn: 想象河水慢慢顶着一道有裂缝的石墙，直到它倒塌。

abstract.en: Picture a person whose smile makes a whole room turn towards them.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人的笑容让整个房间的人都忍不住看过去。

examples.en: The bakery was full of the irresistible smell of fresh bread.
examples.cn: 面包店里满是新鲜面包那令人无法抗拒的香味。

examples.en: To a young player, a place in the first team is irresistible.
examples.cn: 对年轻球员来说，进入一线队的位置是无法抗拒的诱惑。

examples.en: She found the old bookshop irresistible and went in at once.
examples.cn: 她觉得那家旧书店太迷人了，立刻走了进去。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一、resist、able」——一想要 resist（抵抗）都 able（做不到），就是无法抗拒。这只是拆词联想，与构词位置无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ re-（向后）+ sistere（站立）→ resistere（顶住、站住脚）→ resist（抵抗）→ 加形容词后缀 -ible → irresistible，核心义「顶不住、站不稳」。

sensesIntro.en: Irresistible first denies resistance to attraction, then to physical force, then to personal charm, and finally to inner urges.
sensesIntro.cn: irresistible 先指对吸引力无从抵抗，再指对物理力量无从抵挡，继而指人的魅力，最后指内心的冲动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a freshly baked cake placed before a hungry child.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块刚出炉的蛋糕摆在一个饿着肚子的孩子面前。

branches.en: Temptation is the sense that meets daily shopping and food.
branches.cn: 诱惑义对应日常购物与食物场景。

branches.en: Raw force is the older, more literal sense.
branches.cn: 原始力量是更早、更字面的义项。

branches.en: Personal charm moves the same frame to people.
branches.cn: 个人魅力把同一框架移用到人身上。

branches.en: Both an offer and a flood overwhelm a defence that cannot hold.
branches.cn: 报价与洪水都压垮了守不住的防线。

branches.en: Charm outside and desire inside both make resistance impossible.
branches.cn: 外在的魅力与内在的欲望，都让抵抗无从谈起。

intro.en: Irresistible stacks a negative prefix, a Latin verb meaning to stand against, and a suffix meaning able to be.
intro.cn: irresistible 由三层叠成：否定前缀、意为主张对抗的拉丁动词、以及表示「能够被……」的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin sistere, to stand, and its frequentative form resistere, to stand back against something, are the true root of the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sistere（站）及其加强形式 resistere（向后站、顶住），才是整个词族真正的根。
